label: 3DModel
comment: A 3D model represents some kind of 3D content, which may have [[encoding]]s in one or more [[MediaObject]]s. Many 3D formats are available (e.g. see [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category:3D_graphics_file_formats)); specific encoding formats can be represented using the [[encodingFormat]] property applied to the relevant [[MediaObject]]. For the case of a single file published after Zip compression, the convention of appending '+zip' to the [[encodingFormat]] can be used. Geospatial, AR/VR, artistic/animation, gaming, engineering and scientific content can all be represented using [[3DModel]].
enriched_comment: A 3DModel, as a MediaObject under CreativeWork, represents some kind of three-dimensional content, which may have various digital encodings. Also called 3D content, digital model, virtual model. Examples: A CAD file of an engine part, a character model for a video game, a geospatial terrain model, an architectural rendering.
embedding_text: 3DModel (Thing > CreativeWork > MediaObject): A 3DModel, as a MediaObject under CreativeWork, represents some kind of three-dimensional content, which may have various digital encodings. Also called 3D content, digital model, virtual model.

embedding_text: AMRadioChannel (Thing > Intangible > BroadcastChannel > RadioChannel): An AMRadioChannel is a specific type of BroadcastChannel that transmits radio signals using amplitude modulation. Also called AM channel, amplitude modulation radio.

enriched_comment: An AboutPage is a specific type of WebPage dedicated to providing information about an organization, person, or entity. Also called About Us page, company info page, profile page. label: AcceptAction
comment:
The act of committing to/adopting an object.

Related actions:

* [[RejectAction]]: The antonym of AcceptAction.
enriched_comment: AcceptAction, as an AllocateAction, is the act of committing to or adopting an object. Also called approve, agree to, take on, embrace. Examples: Accepting a job offer, accepting terms and conditions, accepting a gift, accepting a proposal. Distinct from RejectAction, which is the antonym of committing to an object.
embedding_text: AcceptAction (Thing > Action > OrganizeAction > AllocateAction): AcceptAction, as an AllocateAction, is the act of committing to or adopting an object. Also called approve, agree to, take on, embrace.

label: Accommodation
comment: An accommodation is a place that can accommodate human beings, e.g. a hotel room, a camping pitch, or a meeting room. Many accommodations are for overnight stays, but this is not a mandatory requirement. For more specific types of accommodations not defined in schema.org, one can use [[additionalType]] with external vocabularies. See also the dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations .
enriched_comment: An Accommodation is a Place that can house human beings, such as a hotel room, camping pitch, or meeting room. Also called lodging, dwelling, living space, temporary residence. Examples: A hotel suite, a campsite, a vacation rental apartment, a conference room.
embedding_text: Accommodation (Thing > Place): An Accommodation is a Place that can house human beings, such as a hotel room, camping pitch, or meeting room. Also called lodging, dwelling, living space, temporary residence.

label: AccountingService
comment: Accountancy business.\n\nAs a [[LocalBusiness]] it can be described as a [[provider]] of one or more [[Service]]\(s).
enriched_comment: An AccountingService is a LocalBusiness that provides accountancy services. Also called accounting firm, bookkeeping service, tax preparation service. Examples: H&R Block, Deloitte Tax Services, a local CPA firm.
embedding_text: AccountingService (Thing > Organization > LocalBusiness > FinancialService): An AccountingService is a LocalBusiness that provides accountancy services. Also called accounting firm, bookkeeping service, tax preparation service.

label: AchieveAction
comment: The act of accomplishing something via previous efforts. It is an instantaneous action rather than an ongoing process.
enriched_comment: AchieveAction is an instantaneous Action representing the accomplishment of something through prior efforts. Also called accomplish, attain, succeed, complete. Examples: Winning a race, graduating from college, reaching a sales target, completing a project.
embedding_text: AchieveAction (Thing > Action): AchieveAction is an instantaneous Action representing the accomplishment of something through prior efforts. Also called accomplish, attain, succeed, complete.

label: Action
comment: An action performed by a direct agent and indirect participants upon a direct object. Optionally happens at a location with the help of an inanimate instrument. The execution of the action may produce a result. Specific action sub-type documentation specifies the exact expectation of each argument/role.\n\nSee also [blog post](https://blog.schema.org/2014/04/16/announcing-schema-org-actions/) and [Actions overview document](https://schema.org/docs/actions.html).
enriched_comment: An Action is a fundamental schema.org type representing an activity performed by an agent, potentially involving objects, participants, locations, and instruments, and producing a result. Also called activity, operation, deed, event. Examples: Reading a book, buying groceries, sending an email, cooking dinner.
embedding_text: Action (Thing): An Action is a fundamental schema.org type representing an activity performed by an agent, potentially involving objects, participants, locations, and instruments, and producing a result. Also called activity, operation, deed, event.

label: ActionAccessSpecification
comment: A set of requirements that must be fulfilled in order to perform an Action.
enriched_comment: An ActionAccessSpecification is an Intangible item detailing the requirements that must be met to perform a specific Action. Also called access requirements, action prerequisites, permission rules. Examples: "Requires login," "Subscription needed," "Age 18+," "Admin privileges."
embedding_text: ActionAccessSpecification (Thing > Intangible): An ActionAccessSpecification is an Intangible item detailing the requirements that must be met to perform a specific Action. Also called access requirements, action prerequisites, permission rules. Examples: "Requires login," "Subscription needed," "Age 18+," "Admin privileges."

label: ActionStatusType
comment: The status of an Action.

embedding_text: ActionStatusType (Thing > Intangible > Enumeration > StatusEnumeration): ActionStatusType is an Enumeration representing the current state or status of an Action. Also called action state, status of action, progress status.

label: ActivateAction
comment: The act of starting or activating a device or application (e.g. starting a timer or turning on a flashlight).
enriched_comment: ActivateAction, as a ControlAction, is the act of starting or turning on a device or application. Also called turn on, start up, enable, initiate. Examples: Turning on a light, starting a timer, activating an alarm, launching an app. Distinct from DeactivateAction, which is the act of stopping or turning off.
embedding_text: ActivateAction (Thing > Action > ControlAction): ActivateAction, as a ControlAction, is the act of starting or turning on a device or application. Also called turn on, start up, enable, initiate.

label: AddAction
comment: The act of editing by adding an object to a collection.
enriched_comment: AddAction, as an UpdateAction, is the act of editing by incorporating an object into a collection. Also called append, include, insert, attach. embedding_text: AddAction (Thing > Action > UpdateAction): AddAction, as an UpdateAction, is the act of editing by incorporating an object into a collection. Also called append, include, insert, attach.

label: AdministrativeArea
comment: A geographical region, typically under the jurisdiction of a particular government.
enriched_comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.
embedding_text: AdministrativeArea (Thing > Place): An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory.

label: AdultEntertainment

enriched_comment: AdultEntertainment is an EntertainmentBusiness specializing in content or services intended for adults. Also called adult venue, adult club, adult establishment. Examples: A strip club, an adult movie theater, an adult bookstore.
embedding_text: AdultEntertainment (Thing > Organization > LocalBusiness > EntertainmentBusiness): AdultEntertainment is an EntertainmentBusiness specializing in content or services intended for adults. Also called adult venue, adult club, adult establishment.

enriched_comment: AdultOrientedEnumeration is an Enumeration of factors that make a product or content relevant or potentially restricted for adults only. label: AdvertiserContentArticle
comment: An [[Article]] that an external entity has paid to place or to produce to its specifications. Includes [advertorials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advertorial), sponsored content, native advertising and other paid content.
enriched_comment: An AdvertiserContentArticle is an Article that has been paid for or produced to the specifications of an external entity. Also called sponsored article, advertorial, native advertising, paid content. Examples: A blog post promoting a product written by an influencer, a sponsored news segment, an article funded by a brand. Distinct from NewsArticle, which is typically produced by independent journalists.
embedding_text: AdvertiserContentArticle (Thing > CreativeWork > Article): An AdvertiserContentArticle is an Article that has been paid for or produced to the specifications of an external entity. Also called sponsored article, advertorial, native advertising, paid content.

label: AggregateOffer
comment: When a single product is associated with multiple offers (for example, the same pair of shoes is offered by different merchants), then AggregateOffer can be used.\n\nNote: AggregateOffers are normally expected to associate multiple offers that all share the same defined [[businessFunction]] value, or default to http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Sell if businessFunction is not explicitly defined.
enriched_comment: An AggregateOffer is an Offer that groups multiple individual offers for the same product or service, often from different merchants. Also called bundled offers, collective offer, multiple offers. Examples: A product page showing prices from several retailers, a flight search result listing different airline prices, a comparison shopping result. Distinct from Offer, which represents a single offer for a product or service.
embedding_text: AggregateOffer (Thing > Intangible > Offer): An AggregateOffer is an Offer that groups multiple individual offers for the same product or service, often from different merchants. Also called bundled offers, collective offer, multiple offers.

label: AggregateRating
comment: The average rating based on multiple ratings or reviews.
enriched_comment: An AggregateRating is a Rating that represents the average or summary of multiple individual ratings or reviews. Also called average rating, collective rating, summary score, overall rating. Examples: A product's 4.5-star rating based on 100 reviews, a movie's Rotten Tomatoes score, a restaurant's Yelp rating. Distinct from Rating, which is a single individual rating.
embedding_text: AggregateRating (Thing > Intangible > Rating): An AggregateRating is a Rating that represents the average or summary of multiple individual ratings or reviews. Also called average rating, collective rating, summary score, overall rating.

label: AgreeAction
comment: The act of expressing a consistency of opinion with the object. An agent agrees to/about an object (a proposition, topic or theme) with participants.
enriched_comment: AgreeAction, as a ReactAction, is the act of expressing a consistency of opinion with an object or proposition. Also called concur, assent, approve, consent. Examples: Agreeing with a statement, consenting to a proposal, approving a plan, liking a social media post. Distinct from DisagreeAction, which is the act of expressing an inconsistency of opinion.
embedding_text: AgreeAction (Thing > Action > AssessAction > ReactAction): AgreeAction, as a ReactAction, is the act of expressing a consistency of opinion with an object or proposition. Also called concur, assent, approve, consent.

label: Airline
comment: An organization that provides flights for passengers.
enriched_comment: An Airline is an Organization that provides air transportation services for passengers. Also called air carrier, air transport company, flight operator. Examples: United Airlines, British Airways, Lufthansa, Southwest Airlines. Distinct from Airport, which is the facility where planes take off and land.
embedding_text: Airline (Thing > Organization): An Airline is an Organization that provides air transportation services for passengers. Also called air carrier, air transport company, flight operator.

label: Airport
comment: An airport.
enriched_comment: An Airport is a CivicStructure that serves as a facility for aircraft to take off and land, and for passenger and cargo services. Also called airfield, aerodrome, air terminal. Examples: London Heathrow Airport, John F. Kennedy International Airport, Tokyo Narita Airport. Distinct from Airline, which is the company operating flights.
embedding_text: Airport (Thing > Place > CivicStructure): An Airport is a CivicStructure that serves as a facility for aircraft to take off and land, and for passenger and cargo services. Also called airfield, aerodrome, air terminal. Kennedy International Airport, Tokyo Narita Airport.

label: AlignmentObject
comment: An intangible item that describes an alignment between a learning resource and a node in an educational framework. Should not be used where the nature of the alignment can be described using a simple property, for example to express that a resource [[teaches]] or [[assesses]] a competency.
enriched_comment: An AlignmentObject is an Intangible item describing a relationship or correspondence between a learning resource and a node in an educational framework. Also called learning alignment, competency mapping, educational standard link. Examples: A resource aligned to a specific Common Core State Standard, a course module mapped to a learning outcome, a textbook chapter linked to a curriculum objective.
embedding_text: AlignmentObject (Thing > Intangible): An AlignmentObject is an Intangible item describing a relationship or correspondence between a learning resource and a node in an educational framework. Also called learning alignment, competency mapping, educational standard link.

label: AllocateAction
comment: The act of organizing tasks/objects/events by associating resources to it.
enriched_comment: AllocateAction, as an OrganizeAction, is the act of assigning resources to tasks, objects, or events. Also called assign, designate, distribute, earmark. Examples: Allocating budget to a project, assigning staff to a task, reserving a room for a meeting, distributing supplies.
embedding_text: AllocateAction (Thing > Action > OrganizeAction): AllocateAction, as an OrganizeAction, is the act of assigning resources to tasks, objects, or events. Also called assign, designate, distribute, earmark.

label: AmpStory

enriched_comment: An AmpStory is a CreativeWork with a visual storytelling format designed for online viewing, especially on mobile devices. Also called AMP Web Story, visual story, mobile story. Examples: A Google AMP Story about a travel destination, a news publisher's visual story, a brand's product showcase story.
embedding_text: AmpStory (Thing > CreativeWork): An AmpStory is a CreativeWork with a visual storytelling format designed for online viewing, especially on mobile devices. Also called AMP Web Story, visual story, mobile story.

label: AmusementPark
comment: An amusement park.

embedding_text: AmusementPark (Thing > Organization > LocalBusiness > EntertainmentBusiness): An AmusementPark is an EntertainmentBusiness offering rides, attractions, and other forms of entertainment. Also called theme park, funfair, carnival.

label: AnalysisNewsArticle
comment: An AnalysisNewsArticle is a [[NewsArticle]] that, while based on factual reporting, incorporates the expertise of the author/producer, offering interpretations and conclusions.
enriched_comment: An AnalysisNewsArticle is a NewsArticle that combines factual reporting with the author's expertise, offering interpretations and conclusions. Also called news analysis, interpretive news, expert commentary. Examples: An article analyzing the economic impact of a new policy, a piece interpreting election results, a report on scientific findings with expert commentary. Distinct from NewsArticle, which primarily focuses on factual reporting without extensive interpretation.
embedding_text: AnalysisNewsArticle (Thing > CreativeWork > Article > NewsArticle): An AnalysisNewsArticle is a NewsArticle that combines factual reporting with the author's expertise, offering interpretations and conclusions. Also called news analysis, interpretive news, expert commentary.

label: AnatomicalStructure
comment: Any part of the human body, typically a component of an anatomical system. Organs, tissues, and cells are all anatomical structures.
enriched_comment: An AnatomicalStructure is a MedicalEntity representing any part of the human body, such as organs, tissues, or cells. Also called body part, biological structure, anatomical component. Examples: The heart, a bone, a muscle, a neuron, the liver. Distinct from AnatomicalSystem, which is a group of structures working together.
embedding_text: AnatomicalStructure (Thing > MedicalEntity): An AnatomicalStructure is a MedicalEntity representing any part of the human body, such as organs, tissues, or cells. Also called body part, biological structure, anatomical component.

label: AnatomicalSystem
comment: An anatomical system is a group of anatomical structures that work together to perform a certain task. Anatomical systems, such as organ systems, are one organizing principle of anatomy, and can include circulatory, digestive, endocrine, integumentary, immune, lymphatic, muscular, nervous, reproductive, respiratory, skeletal, urinary, vestibular, and other systems.
enriched_comment: An AnatomicalSystem is a MedicalEntity comprising a group of anatomical structures that function together to perform a specific task. Also called organ system, biological system, body system. Examples: The circulatory system, the digestive system, the nervous system, the skeletal system. Distinct from AnatomicalStructure, which is an individual part of the body.
embedding_text: AnatomicalSystem (Thing > MedicalEntity): An AnatomicalSystem is a MedicalEntity comprising a group of anatomical structures that function together to perform a specific task. Also called organ system, biological system, body system.

label: AnimalShelter
comment: Animal shelter.
enriched_comment: An AnimalShelter is a LocalBusiness that provides temporary housing and care for animals, often facilitating adoption. Also called animal rescue, humane society, pet shelter. Examples: The ASPCA, a local humane society, a dog rescue organization.
embedding_text: AnimalShelter (Thing > Organization > LocalBusiness): An AnimalShelter is a LocalBusiness that provides temporary housing and care for animals, often facilitating adoption. Also called animal rescue, humane society, pet shelter.

label: Answer
comment: An answer offered to a question; perhaps correct, perhaps opinionated or wrong.
enriched_comment: An Answer is a CreativeWork that is a Comment, specifically a response offered to a question. Also called reply, response, solution, explanation. Examples: a student's answer on a test, a user's reply to a forum post, a doctor's diagnosis, a riddle's solution.
embedding_text: Answer (Thing > CreativeWork > Comment): An Answer is a CreativeWork that is a Comment, specifically a response offered to a question. Also called reply, response, solution, explanation.

label: Apartment
comment: An apartment (in American English) or flat (in British English) is a self-contained housing unit (a type of residential real estate) that occupies only part of a building (source: Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia, see http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apartment ).
enriched_comment: An Apartment is a self-contained housing unit, a type of residential real estate that occupies only part of a building. Also called flat, condo, dwelling unit, residential unit. Examples: a studio apartment, a two-bedroom flat, a penthouse suite, a loft. Distinct from ApartmentComplex, which is a building containing multiple apartments.
embedding_text: Apartment (Thing > Place > Accommodation): An Apartment is a self-contained housing unit, a type of residential real estate that occupies only part of a building. Also called flat, condo, dwelling unit, residential unit.

label: ApartmentComplex
comment: Residence type: Apartment complex.
enriched_comment: An ApartmentComplex is a Residence consisting of a building or group of buildings containing multiple individual apartment units. Also called residential complex, flat complex, housing estate. Examples: The Grand Apartments, Sunset Towers, a student housing complex, a condominium development. Distinct from Apartment, which is a single housing unit within a complex.
embedding_text: ApartmentComplex (Thing > Place > Residence): An ApartmentComplex is a Residence consisting of a building or group of buildings containing multiple individual apartment units. Also called residential complex, flat complex, housing estate.

label: AppendAction
comment: The act of inserting at the end if an ordered collection.
enriched_comment: An AppendAction is an InsertAction that specifically involves adding an item to the end of an ordered collection. Also called add to end, suffix, concatenate, tack on. Examples: adding a new item to the end of a shopping list, appending a chapter to a book, adding a new log entry to a file, joining two strings.
embedding_text: AppendAction (Thing > Action > UpdateAction > AddAction > InsertAction): An AppendAction is an InsertAction that specifically involves adding an item to the end of an ordered collection. Also called add to end, suffix, concatenate, tack on.

label: ApplyAction
comment:
The act of registering to an organization/service without the guarantee to receive it.

Related actions:

* [[RegisterAction]]: Unlike RegisterAction, ApplyAction has no guarantees that the application will be accepted.
enriched_comment: An ApplyAction is an OrganizeAction representing the act of formally requesting to join an organization or receive a service, without a guarantee of acceptance. Also called submit application, make a request, seek admission, bid for. Examples: applying for a job, submitting a college application, applying for a loan, requesting a permit. Distinct from RegisterAction, which implies a successful enrollment or sign-up.
embedding_text: ApplyAction (Thing > Action > OrganizeAction): An ApplyAction is an OrganizeAction representing the act of formally requesting to join an organization or receive a service, without a guarantee of acceptance. Also called submit application, make a request, seek admission, bid for.

label: ApprovedIndication
comment: An indication for a medical therapy that has been formally specified or approved by a regulatory body that regulates use of the therapy; for example, the US FDA approves indications for most drugs in the US.
enriched_comment: An ApprovedIndication is a MedicalIndication for a therapy that has been formally specified and sanctioned by a regulatory body. Also called sanctioned use, authorized indication, regulatory approval, official use. Examples: FDA-approved use of a drug for a specific disease, a medical device's CE mark for a particular procedure, a vaccine's approved age range.
embedding_text: ApprovedIndication (Thing > MedicalEntity > MedicalIndication): An ApprovedIndication is a MedicalIndication for a therapy that has been formally specified and sanctioned by a regulatory body. Also called sanctioned use, authorized indication, regulatory approval, official use.

label: Aquarium
comment: Aquarium.
enriched_comment: An Aquarium is a CivicStructure, typically a public facility, where aquatic animals and plants are kept and displayed. Also called public aquarium, marine life center, oceanarium. Examples: Monterey Bay Aquarium, Georgia Aquarium, a local fish exhibit.
embedding_text: Aquarium (Thing > Place > CivicStructure): An Aquarium is a CivicStructure, typically a public facility, where aquatic animals and plants are kept and displayed. Also called public aquarium, marine life center, oceanarium.

label: ArchiveComponent

enriched_comment: An ArchiveComponent is an intangible CreativeWork representing any content within an archive, whether an individual item or a collection, described by specific archival properties. embedding_text: ArchiveComponent (Thing > CreativeWork): An ArchiveComponent is an intangible CreativeWork representing any content within an archive, whether an individual item or a collection, described by specific archival properties. label: ArchiveOrganization
comment: An organization with archival holdings. An organization which keeps and preserves archival material and typically makes it accessible to the public.
enriched_comment: An ArchiveOrganization is a LocalBusiness that maintains, preserves, and typically provides public access to archival materials. Also called archives, historical society, records center, repository. Examples: National Archives, a university special collections library, a corporate archive, a local historical society.
embedding_text: ArchiveOrganization (Thing > Organization > LocalBusiness): An ArchiveOrganization is a LocalBusiness that maintains, preserves, and typically provides public access to archival materials. Also called archives, historical society, records center, repository.

label: ArriveAction
comment: The act of arriving at a place. An agent arrives at a destination from a fromLocation, optionally with participants.
enriched_comment: An ArriveAction is a MoveAction representing the act of an agent reaching a specific destination from a starting location. Also called reach destination, get to, land, pull in. embedding_text: ArriveAction (Thing > Action > MoveAction): An ArriveAction is a MoveAction representing the act of an agent reaching a specific destination from a starting location. Also called reach destination, get to, land, pull in.

label: ArtGallery
comment: An art gallery.
enriched_comment: An ArtGallery is an EntertainmentBusiness that displays and often sells works of art. Also called gallery, art exhibition space, fine art dealer. Examples: The Louvre, a local contemporary art gallery, a commercial art dealership, a pop-up exhibition space.
embedding_text: ArtGallery (Thing > Organization > LocalBusiness > EntertainmentBusiness): An ArtGallery is an EntertainmentBusiness that displays and often sells works of art. Also called gallery, art exhibition space, fine art dealer.

label: Artery
comment: A type of blood vessel that specifically carries blood away from the heart.
enriched_comment: An Artery is a Vessel, a type of blood vessel that specifically transports blood away from the heart. Also called blood artery, arterial vessel. Examples: aorta, pulmonary artery, carotid artery, femoral artery. Distinct from Vein, which carries blood towards the heart.
embedding_text: Artery (Thing > MedicalEntity > AnatomicalStructure > Vessel): An Artery is a Vessel, a type of blood vessel that specifically transports blood away from the heart. Also called blood artery, arterial vessel.

label: Article
comment: An article, such as a news article or piece of investigative report. Newspapers and magazines have articles of many different types and this is intended to cover them all.\n\nSee also [blog post](https://blog.schema.org/2014/09/02/schema-org-support-for-bibliographic-relationships-and-periodicals/).
enriched_comment: An Article is a CreativeWork, typically a written piece such as a news report, magazine feature, or investigative report. Also called written piece, report, feature, essay, column. Examples: a newspaper article about local politics, a magazine feature on travel, a scientific journal article, a blog post. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is a specific type of article published on a blog.
embedding_text: Article (Thing > CreativeWork): An Article is a CreativeWork, typically a written piece such as a news report, magazine feature, or investigative report. Also called written piece, report, feature, essay, column.

label: AskAction
comment:
The act of posing a question / favor to someone.

Related actions:

* [[ReplyAction]]: Appears generally as a response to AskAction.
enriched_comment: An AskAction is a CommunicateAction representing the act of posing a question or requesting a favor from someone. Also called inquire, query, request, solicit. Examples: asking for directions, posing a question in a Q&A forum, requesting help from a colleague, asking for a donation. Distinct from ReplyAction, which is a response to a question or request.
embedding_text: AskAction (Thing > Action > InteractAction > CommunicateAction): An AskAction is a CommunicateAction representing the act of posing a question or requesting a favor from someone. Also called inquire, query, request, solicit.

label: AskPublicNewsArticle
comment: A [[NewsArticle]] expressing an open call by a [[NewsMediaOrganization]] asking the public for input, insights, clarifications, anecdotes, documentation, etc., on an issue, for reporting purposes.
enriched_comment: An AskPublicNewsArticle is a NewsArticle that serves as an open call from a news organization, soliciting input, insights, or documentation from the public for reporting purposes. Examples: a newspaper asking readers for stories about a local event, a news site requesting photos from a natural disaster, a journalist seeking expert opinions on a topic.
embedding_text: AskPublicNewsArticle (Thing > CreativeWork > Article > NewsArticle): An AskPublicNewsArticle is a NewsArticle that serves as an open call from a news organization, soliciting input, insights, or documentation from the public for reporting purposes. Also called public appeal article, crowdsourced news request, call for information.

label: AssessAction

Examples: a critic reviewing a movie, a teacher grading an assignment, a user rating a product, a doctor evaluating a patient's condition.
embedding_text: AssessAction (Thing > Action): An AssessAction is an Action involving the formation of an opinion, reaction, or sentiment about something. Also called evaluate, appraise, judge, review, rate.

label: AssignAction
comment: The act of allocating an action/event/task to some destination (someone or something).

Also called delegate, allocate, task, designate, appoint. Examples: assigning homework to students, delegating a task to an employee, assigning a case to a lawyer, designating a role in a project.
embedding_text: AssignAction (Thing > Action > OrganizeAction > AllocateAction): An AssignAction is an AllocateAction representing the act of allocating an action, event, or task to a specific person or entity. Also called delegate, allocate, task, designate, appoint.

label: Atlas
comment: A collection or bound volume of maps, charts, plates or tables, physical or in media form illustrating any subject.

label: Campground
comment:
A camping site, campsite, or [[Campground]] is a place used for overnight stay in the outdoors, typically containing individual [[CampingPitch]] locations. 

 In British English a campsite is an area, usually divided into a number of pitches, where people can camp overnight using tents or camper vans or caravans; this British English use of the word is synonymous with the American English expression campground. In American English the term campsite generally means an area where an individual, family, group, or military unit can pitch a tent or park a camper; a campground may contain many campsites (source: Wikipedia, see [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campsite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campsite)).

 See also the dedicated [document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations](/docs/hotels.html).
enriched_comment: A Campground is a CivicStructure or place used for overnight outdoor stays, typically containing multiple individual camping pitches for tents or recreational vehicles. Also called camping site, campsite, RV park, caravan park. Examples: Yellowstone National Park Campground, KOA Campground, a local state park campsite. Distinct from Hotel, which provides indoor lodging.
embedding_text: Campground (Thing > Place > CivicStructure): A Campground is a CivicStructure or place used for overnight outdoor stays, typically containing multiple individual camping pitches for tents or recreational vehicles. Also called camping site, campsite, RV park, caravan park.

label: CampingPitch
comment:
A [[CampingPitch]] is an individual place for overnight stay in the outdoors, typically being part of a larger camping site, or [[Campground]].

 In British English a campsite, or campground, is an area, usually divided into a number of pitches, where people can camp overnight using tents or camper vans or caravans; this British English use of the word is synonymous with the American English expression campground. In American English the term campsite generally means an area where an individual, family, group, or military unit can pitch a tent or park a camper; a campground may contain many campsites. (Source: Wikipedia, see [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campsite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campsite).)

 See also the dedicated [document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations](/docs/hotels.html).
enriched_comment: An individual outdoor space for overnight stay, typically part of a larger camping site or campground. Also called tent pitch, RV pitch, caravan pitch, campsite spot. Examples: Tent site #3 at Yosemite, RV spot at KOA, a designated area for a caravan. Distinct from Campground, which is the larger site containing multiple pitches.
embedding_text: CampingPitch (Thing > Place > Accommodation): An individual outdoor space for overnight stay, typically part of a larger camping site or campground. Also called tent pitch, RV pitch, caravan pitch, campsite spot.

A certification is typically issued by an indendent certification body, for example a professional organization or government. It formally attests certain characteristics about the subject, for example Organizations can be ISO certified, Food products can be certified Organic or Vegan, a Person can be a certified professional, a Place can be certified for food processing. There are certifications for many domains: regulatory, organizational, recycling, food, efficiency, educational, ecological, etc. A certification is a form of credential, as are accreditations and licenses. Mapped from the [gs1:CertificationDetails](https://www.gs1.org/voc/CertificationDetails) class in the GS1 Web Vocabulary.

label: CheckInAction
comment:
The act of an agent communicating (service provider, social media, etc) their arrival by registering/confirming for a previously reserved service (e.g. flight check-in) or at a place (e.g. hotel), possibly resulting in a result (boarding pass, etc).

Related actions:

* [[CheckOutAction]]: The antonym of CheckInAction.
* [[ArriveAction]]: Unlike ArriveAction, CheckInAction implies that the agent is informing/confirming the start of a previously reserved service.
* [[ConfirmAction]]: Unlike ConfirmAction, CheckInAction implies that the agent is informing/confirming the *start* of a previously reserved service rather than its validity/existence.

Examples: Checking into a hotel, checking in for a flight, checking in at a conference. Distinct from ArriveAction, which is simply arriving without prior reservation confirmation.

label: CheckOutAction

* [[DepartAction]]: Unlike DepartAction, CheckOutAction implies that the agent is informing/confirming the end of a previously reserved service.

enriched_comment: The act of an agent communicating their departure from a previously reserved service or place. Also called depart, sign out, settle bill. label: Claim
comment: A [[Claim]] in Schema.org represents a specific, factually-oriented claim that could be the [[itemReviewed]] in a [[ClaimReview]]. The content of a claim can be summarized with the [[text]] property. Variations on well known claims can have their common identity indicated via [[sameAs]] links, and summarized with a [[name]]. Ideally, a [[Claim]] description includes enough contextual information to minimize the risk of ambiguity or inclarity. In practice, many claims are better understood in the context in which they appear or the interpretations provided by claim reviews. Beyond [[ClaimReview]], the Claim type can be associated with related creative works - for example a [[ScholarlyArticle]] or [[Question]] might be [[about]] some [[Claim]]. At this time, Schema.org does not define any types of relationship between claims. This is a natural area for future exploration.
enriched_comment: A specific, factually-oriented statement that can be reviewed for accuracy. Also called assertion, statement, proposition, contention. Examples: "The Earth is flat," "Coffee cures cancer," "This product is 100% organic." Distinct from ClaimReview, which is the review of a claim.

embedding_text: ClaimReview (Thing > CreativeWork > Review): A creative work that provides a fact-checking review of a specific claim. Also called fact-check, debunking, truth verification.

label: CompleteDataFeed
comment: A [[CompleteDataFeed]] is a [[DataFeed]] whose standard representation includes content for every item currently in the feed. This is the equivalent of Atom's element as defined in Feed Paging and Archiving [RFC 5005](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5005), for example (and as defined for Atom), when using data from a feed that represents a collection of items that varies over time (e.g. "Top Twenty Records") there is no need to have newer entries mixed in alongside older, obsolete entries. By marking this feed as a CompleteDataFeed, old entries can be safely discarded when the feed is refreshed, since we can assume the feed has provided descriptions for all current items.
enriched_comment: A data feed whose standard representation includes all current items, allowing older entries to be safely discarded upon refresh. Also called full data feed, comprehensive feed, complete item feed. Examples: An Atom feed of "Top Twenty Records" where all current records are present, a product catalog feed that always contains all available products, a news feed that provides all current articles. Distinct from DataFeed, which is a general feed that might only contain updates or partial information.
embedding_text: CompleteDataFeed (Thing > CreativeWork > Dataset > DataFeed): A data feed whose standard representation includes all current items, allowing older entries to be safely discarded upon refresh. Also called full data feed, comprehensive feed, complete item feed.

label: CreativeWorkSeries
comment:
A CreativeWorkSeries in schema.org is a group of related items, typically but not necessarily of the same kind. CreativeWorkSeries are usually organized into some order, often chronological. Unlike [[ItemList]] which is a general purpose data structure for lists of things, the emphasis with CreativeWorkSeries is on published materials (written e.g. books and periodicals, or media such as TV, radio and games).

Specific subtypes are available for describing [[TVSeries]], [[RadioSeries]], [[MovieSeries]], [[BookSeries]], [[Periodical]] and [[VideoGameSeries]]. In each case, the [[hasPart]] / [[isPartOf]] properties can be used to relate the CreativeWorkSeries to its parts. The general CreativeWorkSeries type serves largely just to organize these more specific and practical subtypes.

It is common for properties applicable to an item from the series to be usefully applied to the containing group. Schema.org attempts to anticipate some of these cases, but publishers should be free to apply properties of the series parts to the series as a whole wherever they seem appropriate.
enriched_comment: A CreativeWorkSeries is an ordered collection of related published materials, such as books, periodicals, TV shows, or video games. Also called series, collection, franchise, saga. Examples: "Harry Potter" book series, "Star Wars" movie series, "The Simpsons" TV series, "The Legend of Zelda" video game series. Distinct from CreativeWorkSeason, which is a single installment within a series.
embedding_text: CreativeWorkSeries (Thing > CreativeWork): A CreativeWorkSeries is an ordered collection of related published materials, such as books, periodicals, TV shows, or video games. Also called series, collection, franchise, saga.

label: CriticReview
comment: A [[CriticReview]] is a more specialized form of Review written or published by a source that is recognized for its reviewing activities. These can include online columns, travel and food guides, TV and radio shows, blogs and other independent Web sites. [[CriticReview]]s are typically more in-depth and professionally written. For simpler, casually written user/visitor/viewer/customer reviews, it is more appropriate to use the [[UserReview]] type. label: Date

embedding_text: DateTime: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime.

label: DatedMoneySpecification

label: DayOfWeek

embedding_text: DayOfWeek (Thing > Intangible > Enumeration): An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name.

label: DaySpa

embedding_text: DaySpa (Thing > Organization > LocalBusiness > HealthAndBeautyBusiness): A local business offering health and beauty services, typically without overnight accommodation. Also called Spa, beauty spa, wellness center.

label: DeactivateAction

embedding_text: DeactivateAction (Thing > Action > ControlAction): An action that involves stopping or turning off a device, application, or process. Also called Turn off, disable, shut down, stop.

label: DefenceEstablishment

embedding_text: DefenceEstablishment (Thing > Place > CivicStructure > GovernmentBuilding): A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station.

label: DefinedRegion

Properties are provided for defining a region by reference to sets of postal codes. Examples: a delivery destination when shopping. Region where regional pricing is configured. Requirement 1: Country: US States: "NY", "CA" Requirement 2: Country: US PostalCode Set: { [94000-94585], [97000, 97999], [13000, 13599]} { [12345, 12345], [78945, 78945], } Region = state, canton, prefecture, autonomous community...
enriched_comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.
embedding_text: DefinedRegion (Thing > Place): A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory.

label: DefinedTerm

label: DeliveryMethod

Commonly used values:

* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModeDirectDownload
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModeFreight
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModeMail
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModeOwnFleet
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModePickUp
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DHL
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#FederalExpress

label: EventSeries
comment: A series of [[Event]]s. Included events can relate with the series using the [[superEvent]] property. An EventSeries is a collection of events that share some unifying characteristic. For example, "The Olympic Games" is a series, which is repeated regularly. The "2012 London Olympics" can be presented both as an [[Event]] in the series "Olympic Games", and as an [[EventSeries]] that included a number of sporting competitions as Events. The nature of the association between the events in an [[EventSeries]] can vary, but typical examples could include a thematic event series (e.g. topical meetups or classes), or a series of regular events that share a location, attendee group and/or organizers. EventSeries has been defined as a kind of Event to make it easy for publishers to use it in an Event context without worrying about which kinds of series are really event-like enough to call an Event. In general an EventSeries may seem more Event-like when the period of time is compact and when aspects such as location are fixed, but it may also sometimes prove useful to describe a longer-term series as an Event.

Also called event cycle, recurring event, series of events. Examples: The Olympic Games, a monthly book club meeting, a season of a concert series, a weekly farmers market.

label: FollowAction
comment:
The act of forming a personal connection with someone/something (object) unidirectionally/asymmetrically to get updates polled from.

Related actions:

* [[BefriendAction]]: Unlike BefriendAction, FollowAction implies that the connection is *not* necessarily reciprocal.
* [[SubscribeAction]]: Unlike SubscribeAction, FollowAction implies that the follower acts as an active agent constantly/actively polling for updates.
* [[RegisterAction]]: Unlike RegisterAction, FollowAction implies that the agent is interested in continuing receiving updates from the object.
* [[JoinAction]]: Unlike JoinAction, FollowAction implies that the agent is interested in getting updates from the object.
* [[TrackAction]]: Unlike TrackAction, FollowAction refers to the polling of updates of all aspects of animate objects rather than the location of inanimate objects (e.g. you track a package, but you don't follow it).
enriched_comment: FollowAction is an InteractAction representing the act of forming a unidirectional personal connection with someone or something to receive updates. Also called subscribe, track, observe. Examples: Following a celebrity on social media, subscribing to a news feed, observing a public figure's activities. Distinct from BefriendAction, which implies a reciprocal connection.
embedding_text: FollowAction (Thing > Action > InteractAction): FollowAction is an InteractAction representing the act of forming a unidirectional personal connection with someone or something to receive updates. Also called subscribe, track, observe.

label: HyperToc
comment: A HyperToc represents a hypertext table of contents for complex media objects, such as [[VideoObject]], [[AudioObject]]. Items in the table of contents are indicated using the [[tocEntry]] property, and typed [[HyperTocEntry]]. For cases where the same larger work is split into multiple files, [[associatedMedia]] can be used on individual [[HyperTocEntry]] items.
enriched_comment: A HyperToc is a creative work representing a hypertext table of contents for complex media objects like videos or audio, with entries indicating specific sections. Also called interactive table of contents, media chapter list, navigable index. Examples: a chapter list for a long documentary video, an interactive index for an audio lecture series.
embedding_text: HyperToc (Thing > CreativeWork): A HyperToc is a creative work representing a hypertext table of contents for complex media objects like videos or audio, with entries indicating specific sections. Also called interactive table of contents, media chapter list, navigable index.

label: HyperTocEntry
comment: A HyperToEntry is an item within a [[HyperToc]], which represents a hypertext table of contents for complex media objects, such as [[VideoObject]], [[AudioObject]]. The media object itself is indicated using [[associatedMedia]]. Each section of interest within that content can be described with a [[HyperTocEntry]], with associated [[startOffset]] and [[endOffset]]. When several entries are all from the same file, [[associatedMedia]] is used on the overarching [[HyperTocEntry]]; if the content has been split into multiple files, they can be referenced using [[associatedMedia]] on each [[HyperTocEntry]].
enriched_comment: A HyperTocEntry is a creative work representing an individual item or section within a HyperToc, specifying its associated media and time offsets. Also called table of contents item, media chapter, section marker. Examples: 'Introduction (0:00-5:30)', 'Keynote Speech (10:15-30:00)', 'Q&A Session (30:00-45:00)'.
embedding_text: HyperTocEntry (Thing > CreativeWork): A HyperTocEntry is a creative work representing an individual item or section within a HyperToc, specifying its associated media and time offsets. Also called table of contents item, media chapter, section marker.

label: ImageObjectSnapshot
comment: A specific and exact (byte-for-byte) version of an [[ImageObject]]. Two byte-for-byte identical files, for the purposes of this type, considered identical. Different external facts about the files, e.g. creator or dateCreated that aren't represented in their actual content, do not affect this notion of identity.

embedding_text: ImageObjectSnapshot (Thing > CreativeWork > MediaObject > ImageObject): An ImageObjectSnapshot is a specific, byte-for-byte identical version of an ImageObject, where identity is determined by the exact content including embedded metadata. enriched_comment: InfectiousAgentClass is a medical enumeration of classes of agents or pathogens that transmit infectious diseases. Also called pathogen type, disease agent category, microbial class. Examples: 'Bacteria', 'Virus', 'Fungus', 'Parasite'.
embedding_text: InfectiousAgentClass (Thing > Intangible > Enumeration > MedicalEnumeration): InfectiousAgentClass is a medical enumeration of classes of agents or pathogens that transmit infectious diseases. Also called pathogen type, disease agent category, microbial class.

label: InfectiousDisease
comment: An infectious disease is a clinically evident human disease resulting from the presence of pathogenic microbial agents, like pathogenic viruses, pathogenic bacteria, fungi, protozoa, multicellular parasites, and prions. To be considered an infectious disease, such pathogens are known to be able to cause this disease.
enriched_comment: An InfectiousDisease is a medical condition resulting from the presence of pathogenic microbial agents like viruses, bacteria, or fungi. Also called communicable disease, contagious illness, infection. Examples: influenza, COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis. Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is a broader category for any health problem.
embedding_text: InfectiousDisease (Thing > MedicalEntity > MedicalCondition): An InfectiousDisease is a medical condition resulting from the presence of pathogenic microbial agents like viruses, bacteria, or fungi. Also called communicable disease, contagious illness, infection.

label: InformAction
comment: The act of notifying someone of information pertinent to them, with no expectation of a response.
enriched_comment: An InformAction is a communicate action representing the act of notifying someone of pertinent information without expecting a response. Also called notify action, announce action, advise action. Examples: sending a broadcast email, posting a public announcement, informing a colleague about a meeting change. Distinct from AskAction, which seeks information, and ReplyAction, which responds to communication.
embedding_text: InformAction (Thing > Action > InteractAction > CommunicateAction): An InformAction is a communicate action representing the act of notifying someone of pertinent information without expecting a response. Also called notify action, announce action, advise action.

label: InsertAction
comment: The act of adding at a specific location in an ordered collection.
enriched_comment: An InsertAction is an add action representing the act of adding an object at a specific location within an ordered collection. Also called place action, embed action, inject action. Examples: inserting a new paragraph into a document, adding an item to a shopping cart, placing a card into a deck. Distinct from AddAction, which is a more general act of adding without specifying location.
embedding_text: InsertAction (Thing > Action > UpdateAction > AddAction): An InsertAction is an add action representing the act of adding an object at a specific location within an ordered collection. Also called place action, embed action, inject action.

label: InstallAction
comment: The act of installing an application.
enriched_comment: An InstallAction is a consume action representing the act of installing an application or software. Also called set up action, deploy action, load software. Examples: installing a new app on a phone, setting up an operating system, deploying a server application.
embedding_text: InstallAction (Thing > Action > ConsumeAction): An InstallAction is a consume action representing the act of installing an application or software. Also called set up action, deploy action, load software.

label: InstantaneousEvent
comment: An event with no duration, like for instance a computer log entry.
enriched_comment: An InstantaneousEvent is a structured value representing an event with no duration, such as a single point in time. Also called momentary event, point event, discrete occurrence. Examples: a computer log entry, a timestamp, a single click on a webpage. Distinct from Event, which typically has a duration.
embedding_text: InstantaneousEvent (Thing > Intangible > StructuredValue): An InstantaneousEvent is a structured value representing an event with no duration, such as a single point in time. Also called momentary event, point event, discrete occurrence.

embedding_text: InsuranceAgency (Thing > Organization > LocalBusiness > FinancialService): An InsuranceAgency is a financial service local business that provides insurance-related services. Also called insurance broker, insurance provider, insurance firm.

label: Intangible
comment: A utility class that serves as the umbrella for a number of 'intangible' things such as quantities, structured values, etc.
enriched_comment: Intangible is a utility class serving as an umbrella for things that lack physical form, such as quantities, structured values, and concepts. Also called abstract entity, non-physical item, conceptual object. Examples: a number, a permit, a service, a list. Distinct from Thing, which is the root of all types, and CreativeWork, which is a specific type of intangible.
embedding_text: Intangible (Thing): Intangible is a utility class serving as an umbrella for things that lack physical form, such as quantities, structured values, and concepts. Also called abstract entity, non-physical item, conceptual object.

label: Integer
comment: Data type: Integer.
enriched_comment: Integer is a data type representing a whole number without a fractional component. Also called whole number, natural number (if positive), counting number. Examples: 0, 1, -5, 1000. Distinct from Float, which includes decimal values.
embedding_text: Integer (Number): Integer is a data type representing a whole number without a fractional component. Also called whole number, natural number (if positive), counting number.

label: InteractAction

enriched_comment: An InteractAction is an action representing the act of interacting with another person or organization. Also called engagement action, social action, communication action. Examples: communicating, joining, inviting, following. Distinct from CommunicateAction, which is a specific type of interaction focused on information exchange.
embedding_text: InteractAction (Thing > Action): An InteractAction is an action representing the act of interacting with another person or organization. Also called engagement action, social action, communication action.

label: InteractionCounter

embedding_text: InteractionCounter (Thing > Intangible > StructuredValue): An InteractionCounter is a structured value summarizing how users have interacted with a CreativeWork. Also called engagement metric, user interaction count, activity tracker.

label: InternetCafe

enriched_comment: An InternetCafe is a local business providing public access to computers with internet connectivity, often alongside food and beverages. Also called cyber cafe, web cafe, net cafe. Examples: a local internet cafe, a gaming cafe with internet access.
embedding_text: InternetCafe (Thing > Organization > LocalBusiness): An InternetCafe is a local business providing public access to computers with internet connectivity, often alongside food and beverages. Also called cyber cafe, web cafe, net cafe.

label: InvestmentFund
comment: A company or fund that gathers capital from a number of investors to create a pool of money that is then re-invested into stocks, bonds and other assets.
enriched_comment: An InvestmentFund is a financial product service that pools capital from multiple investors to reinvest into various assets like stocks and bonds. Also called mutual fund, hedge fund, pooled investment vehicle. Examples: Vanguard S&P 500 Index Fund, a private equity fund, a real estate investment trust (REIT). Distinct from InvestmentOrDeposit, which is a broader category for financial products requiring fund transfers for potential returns.
embedding_text: InvestmentFund (Thing > Intangible > Service > FinancialProduct > InvestmentOrDeposit): An InvestmentFund is a financial product service that pools capital from multiple investors to reinvest into various assets like stocks and bonds. label: InvestmentOrDeposit

Also called financial investment, savings product, capital placement. Examples: a savings account, a certificate of deposit (CD), a stock market investment. embedding_text: InvestmentOrDeposit (Thing > Intangible > Service > FinancialProduct): An InvestmentOrDeposit is a financial product service that typically requires a client to transfer funds to a financial service in return for potential beneficial financial returns. Also called financial investment, savings product, capital placement.

label: InviteAction

embedding_text: InviteAction (Thing > Action > InteractAction > CommunicateAction): An InviteAction is a communicate action representing the act of asking someone to attend an event. Also called invitation action, request attendance, solicit presence.

label: Invoice

embedding_text: Invoice (Thing > Intangible): An Invoice is an intangible statement detailing the money due for goods or services; a bill. Also called bill, statement of account, charge slip.

label: ItemAvailability

label: ItemList

embedding_text: ItemList (Thing > Intangible): An ItemList is an intangible collection of items of any sort, often ordered or ranked. Also called list, collection, sequence, array.

embedding_text: ItemListOrderType (Thing > Intangible > Enumeration): ItemListOrderType is an enumeration for values indicating how an ordered ItemList is organized. Also called list sorting type, item sequence order, collection arrangement.

label: ItemPage

enriched_comment: An ItemPage is a web page devoted to a single item, such as a particular product or hotel. Also called product page, detail page, single item view. embedding_text: ItemPage (Thing > CreativeWork > WebPage): An ItemPage is a web page devoted to a single item, such as a particular product or hotel. Also called product page, detail page, single item view.

label: JobPosting

embedding_text: JobPosting (Thing > Intangible): A JobPosting is an intangible listing that describes an open position within an organization. Also called job advertisement, employment listing, career opening.

label: JoinAction
comment:
An agent joins an event/group with participants/friends at a location.

Related actions:

* [[RegisterAction]]: Unlike RegisterAction, JoinAction refers to joining a group/team of people.
* [[SubscribeAction]]: Unlike SubscribeAction, JoinAction does not imply that you'll be receiving updates.
* [[FollowAction]]: Unlike FollowAction, JoinAction does not imply that you'll be polling for updates.
enriched_comment: A JoinAction is an interact action where an agent becomes part of an event or group with other participants. Also called participate action, become member, attend action. Examples: joining a club, attending a meeting, becoming a member of a team. Distinct from RegisterAction, which is signing up for a service, and SubscribeAction, which implies receiving updates.
embedding_text: JoinAction (Thing > Action > InteractAction): A JoinAction is an interact action where an agent becomes part of an event or group with other participants. Also called participate action, become member, attend action.

label: Joint
comment: The anatomical location at which two or more bones make contact.
enriched_comment: A Joint is an anatomical structure where two or more bones make contact, facilitating movement or providing stability. Also called articulation, bone joint, anatomical junction. Examples: knee joint, elbow joint, hip joint, shoulder joint. Distinct from Bone, which is a single skeletal component.
embedding_text: Joint (Thing > MedicalEntity > AnatomicalStructure): A Joint is an anatomical structure where two or more bones make contact, facilitating movement or providing stability. Also called articulation, bone joint, anatomical junction.

label: LakeBodyOfWater
comment: A lake (for example, Lake Pontrachain).

Examples: Lake Superior, Lake Tahoe, Lake Pontchartrain. Distinct from River, which is flowing water, and OceanBodyOfWater, which is a large saltwater body.
embedding_text: LakeBodyOfWater (Thing > Place > Landform > BodyOfWater): A LakeBodyOfWater is a landform representing a large body of still water surrounded by land. Also called lake, inland sea, reservoir.

label: Landform
comment: A landform or physical feature. Landform elements include mountains, plains, lakes, rivers, seascape and oceanic waterbody interface features such as bays, peninsulas, seas and so forth, including sub-aqueous terrain features such as submersed mountain ranges, volcanoes, and the great ocean basins.
enriched_comment: A Landform is a place representing a natural physical feature of the Earth's surface. Also called geographical feature, terrain feature, natural formation. Examples: mountain, plain, valley, island, river. Distinct from Place, which is a broader category for any location.
embedding_text: Landform (Thing > Place): A Landform is a place representing a natural physical feature of the Earth's surface. Also called geographical feature, terrain feature, natural formation.

label: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings

embedding_text: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings (Thing > Place): LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings is a place representing an important historical landmark or building. Also called historical site, heritage building, monument.

label: Language

The Language type previously also covered programming languages such as Scheme and Lisp, which are now best represented using [[ComputerLanguage]].

Also called natural tongue, human language, spoken language. Examples: English, Spanish, Mandarin, Arabic. Distinct from ComputerLanguage, which refers to programming languages.
embedding_text: Language (Thing > Intangible): Language is an intangible representing natural languages such as Spanish or English, Also called natural tongue, human language, spoken language.

label: LearningResource
comment: The LearningResource type can be used to indicate [[CreativeWork]]s (whether physical or digital) that have a particular and explicit orientation towards learning, education, skill acquisition, and other educational purposes. [[LearningResource]] is expected to be used as an addition to a primary type such as [[Book]], [[VideoObject]], [[Product]] etc. [[EducationEvent]] serves a similar purpose for event-like things (e.g. a [[Trip]]). A [[LearningResource]] may be created as a result of an [[EducationEvent]], for example by recording one.
enriched_comment: A LearningResource is a creative work explicitly oriented towards learning, education, or skill acquisition. Also called educational material, study resource, instructional content. Examples: a textbook, an online course module, a tutorial video, a practice worksheet. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is a broader category for any creative output.
embedding_text: LearningResource (Thing > CreativeWork): A LearningResource is a creative work explicitly oriented towards learning, education, or skill acquisition. Also called educational material, study resource, instructional content.

label: LeaveAction
comment:
An agent leaves an event / group with participants/friends at a location.

embedding_text: LeaveAction (Thing > Action > InteractAction): A LeaveAction is an interact action where an agent departs from an event or group. Also called depart action, exit action, withdraw action.

label: LinkRole

label: MedicalCause
comment: The causative agent(s) that are responsible for the pathophysiologic process that eventually results in a medical condition, symptom or sign. In this schema, unless otherwise specified this is meant to be the proximate cause of the medical condition, symptom or sign. The proximate cause is defined as the causative agent that most directly results in the medical condition, symptom or sign. For example, the HIV virus could be considered a cause of AIDS. Or in a diagnostic context, if a patient fell and sustained a hip fracture and two days later sustained a pulmonary embolism which eventuated in a cardiac arrest, the cause of the cardiac arrest (the proximate cause) would be the pulmonary embolism and not the fall. Medical causes can include cardiovascular, chemical, dermatologic, endocrine, environmental, gastroenterologic, genetic, hematologic, gynecologic, iatrogenic, infectious, musculoskeletal, neurologic, nutritional, obstetric, oncologic, otolaryngologic, pharmacologic, psychiatric, pulmonary, renal, rheumatologic, toxic, traumatic, or urologic causes; medical conditions can be causes as well.
enriched_comment: A medical entity representing the causative agent(s) responsible for a pathophysiologic process leading to a medical condition, symptom, or sign. Also called etiology, causative factor, underlying reason. Examples: "HIV virus" as a cause of AIDS, "pulmonary embolism" as a cause of cardiac arrest, "bacterial infection".
embedding_text: MedicalCause (Thing > MedicalEntity): A medical entity representing the causative agent(s) responsible for a pathophysiologic process leading to a medical condition, symptom, or sign. Also called etiology, causative factor, underlying reason.

label: MedicalObservationalStudy
comment: An observational study is a type of medical study that attempts to infer the possible effect of a treatment through observation of a cohort of subjects over a period of time. This is in contrast with controlled studies, such as the randomized controlled trials represented by MedicalTrial, where each subject is randomly assigned to a treatment group or a control group before the start of the treatment.

Also called observational research, cohort study, epidemiological study. Examples: a study tracking health outcomes in smokers vs. non-smokers, a study on diet and disease incidence. Distinct from MedicalTrial, where subjects are randomly assigned to treatment groups.
embedding_text: MedicalObservationalStudy (Thing > MedicalEntity > MedicalStudy): A medical study that infers the effect of a treatment by observing a cohort of subjects over time, without investigator control over treatment assignment.
