enriched_comment: A medical entity representing anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing a disease, medical condition, or complication. Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability. Examples: "smoking", "high cholesterol", "family history of heart disease", "obesity". Distinct from MedicalRiskEstimator, which is a tool to calculate risk based on multiple factors.
embedding_text: MedicalRiskFactor (Thing > MedicalEntity): A medical entity representing anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing a disease, medical condition, or complication. Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability.

label: MedicalRiskScore
comment: A simple system that adds up the number of risk factors to yield a score that is associated with prognosis, e.g. CHAD score, TIMI risk score.
enriched_comment: A medical risk estimator that is a simple system summing risk factors to yield a score associated with prognosis. Also called clinical score, prognostic score, risk index. Examples: "CHAD score", "TIMI risk score", "APACHE II score". Distinct from MedicalRiskCalculator, which involves more complex mathematical calculations.
embedding_text: MedicalRiskScore (Thing > MedicalEntity > MedicalRiskEstimator): A medical risk estimator that is a simple system summing risk factors to yield a score associated with prognosis. Also called clinical score, prognostic score, risk index.

label: MedicalScholarlyArticle
comment: A scholarly article in the medical domain.
enriched_comment: A scholarly article specifically within the medical domain. Also called medical journal article, clinical research paper, healthcare publication. Examples: a peer-reviewed article on a new drug, a research paper on surgical techniques, a review article on a disease. Distinct from ScholarlyArticle, which is a broader category for academic papers.
embedding_text: MedicalScholarlyArticle (Thing > CreativeWork > Article > ScholarlyArticle): A scholarly article specifically within the medical domain. Also called medical journal article, clinical research paper, healthcare publication.

label: MedicalSign
comment: Any physical manifestation of a person's medical condition discoverable by objective diagnostic tests or physical examination.
enriched_comment: A medical sign or symptom that is an objective physical manifestation of a medical condition, discoverable by diagnostic tests or physical examination. Also called objective symptom, clinical sign, diagnostic finding. Examples: "fever", "rash", "high blood pressure", "swelling". Distinct from MedicalSymptom, which is subjective and reported by the patient.
embedding_text: MedicalSign (Thing > MedicalEntity > MedicalCondition > MedicalSignOrSymptom): A medical sign or symptom that is an objective physical manifestation of a medical condition, discoverable by diagnostic tests or physical examination. Also called objective symptom, clinical sign, diagnostic finding.

label: MedicalSignOrSymptom
comment: Any feature associated or not with a medical condition. In medicine a symptom is generally subjective while a sign is objective.
enriched_comment: A medical condition representing any feature, objective or subjective, associated with a medical condition. Also called clinical manifestation, health indicator, disease feature. Examples: "pain", "fever", "fatigue", "rash", "nausea". Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is the underlying state itself.
embedding_text: MedicalSignOrSymptom (Thing > MedicalEntity > MedicalCondition): A medical condition representing any feature, objective or subjective, associated with a medical condition. Also called clinical manifestation, health indicator, disease feature.

label: MedicalSpecialty
comment: Any specific branch of medical science or practice. Medical specialities include clinical specialties that pertain to particular organ systems and their respective disease states, as well as allied health specialties. Enumerated type.
enriched_comment: An enumeration representing any specific branch of medical science or practice, including clinical and allied health specialties. Also called medical field, clinical discipline, healthcare area. Examples: "Cardiology", "Pediatrics", "Oncology", "Physical Therapy", "Dentistry".
embedding_text: MedicalSpecialty (Thing > Intangible > Enumeration > MedicalEnumeration): An enumeration representing any specific branch of medical science or practice, including clinical and allied health specialties. Also called medical field, clinical discipline, healthcare area.

label: MedicalStudy
comment: A medical study is an umbrella type covering all kinds of research studies relating to human medicine or health, including observational studies and interventional trials and registries, randomized, controlled or not. When the specific type of study is known, use one of the extensions of this type, such as MedicalTrial or MedicalObservationalStudy. Also, note that this type should be used to mark up data that describes the study itself; to tag an article that publishes the results of a study, use MedicalScholarlyArticle. Note: use the code property of MedicalEntity to store study IDs, e.g. clinicaltrials.gov ID.
enriched_comment: A medical entity that is an umbrella type covering all kinds of research studies relating to human medicine or health. Also called clinical study, health research, medical investigation. Examples: a drug trial, an epidemiological survey, a patient registry. Distinct from MedicalScholarlyArticle, which is the publication of study results, not the study itself.
embedding_text: MedicalStudy (Thing > MedicalEntity): A medical entity that is an umbrella type covering all kinds of research studies relating to human medicine or health. Also called clinical study, health research, medical investigation.

label: MedicalStudyStatus
comment: The status of a medical study. Enumerated type.
enriched_comment: An enumeration representing the status of a medical study. Also called study phase, research status, trial stage. Examples: "Recruiting", "Active, not recruiting", "Completed", "Terminated".
embedding_text: MedicalStudyStatus (Thing > Intangible > Enumeration > MedicalEnumeration): An enumeration representing the status of a medical study. Also called study phase, research status, trial stage.

label: MedicalSymptom
comment: Any complaint sensed and expressed by the patient (therefore defined as subjective) like stomachache, lower-back pain, or fatigue.
enriched_comment: A medical sign or symptom that is a subjective complaint sensed and expressed by the patient. Also called subjective symptom, patient complaint, reported feeling. Examples: "stomachache", "lower-back pain", "fatigue", "headache", "nausea". Distinct from MedicalSign, which is an objective finding.
embedding_text: MedicalSymptom (Thing > MedicalEntity > MedicalCondition > MedicalSignOrSymptom): A medical sign or symptom that is a subjective complaint sensed and expressed by the patient. Also called subjective symptom, patient complaint, reported feeling.

label: MedicalTest
comment: Any medical test, typically performed for diagnostic purposes.
enriched_comment: A medical entity representing any medical test, typically performed for diagnostic purposes. Also called diagnostic test, clinical examination, medical screening. Examples: "blood test", "urine test", "MRI scan", "biopsy", "physical exam".
embedding_text: MedicalTest (Thing > MedicalEntity): A medical entity representing any medical test, typically performed for diagnostic purposes. Also called diagnostic test, clinical examination, medical screening.

label: MedicalTestPanel
comment: Any collection of tests commonly ordered together.
enriched_comment: A medical test that is a collection of tests commonly ordered together. Also called test battery, diagnostic panel, group of tests. Examples: "complete blood count (CBC)", "liver function panel", "metabolic panel". Distinct from MedicalTest, which can be a single test.
embedding_text: MedicalTestPanel (Thing > MedicalEntity > MedicalTest): A medical test that is a collection of tests commonly ordered together. Also called test battery, diagnostic panel, group of tests.

label: MedicalTherapy
comment: Any medical intervention designed to prevent, treat, and cure human diseases and medical conditions, including both curative and palliative therapies. Medical therapies are typically processes of care relying upon pharmacotherapy, behavioral therapy, supportive therapy (with fluid or nutrition for example), or detoxification (e.g. hemodialysis) aimed at improving or preventing a health condition.
enriched_comment: A therapeutic medical procedure designed to prevent, treat, and cure human diseases and medical conditions. Also called medical treatment, healthcare intervention, therapy regimen. Examples: "pharmacotherapy", "behavioral therapy", "supportive therapy", "dialysis". Distinct from MedicalProcedure, which is a broader category including diagnostic procedures.
embedding_text: MedicalTherapy (Thing > MedicalEntity > MedicalProcedure > TherapeuticProcedure): A therapeutic medical procedure designed to prevent, treat, and cure human diseases and medical conditions. Also called medical treatment, healthcare intervention, therapy regimen.

label: MedicalTrial
comment: A medical trial is a type of medical study that uses a scientific process to compare the safety and efficacy of medical therapies or medical procedures. In general, medical trials are controlled and subjects are allocated at random to the different treatment and/or control groups.
enriched_comment: A medical study that uses a scientific process to compare the safety and efficacy of medical therapies or procedures, typically with random allocation to groups. Also called clinical trial, randomized controlled trial, interventional study. Examples: a Phase 3 drug trial, a study comparing two surgical techniques, a vaccine efficacy trial. Distinct from MedicalObservationalStudy, where treatment assignment is not controlled by the investigator.
embedding_text: MedicalTrial (Thing > MedicalEntity > MedicalStudy): A medical study that uses a scientific process to compare the safety and efficacy of medical therapies or procedures, typically with random allocation to groups. Also called clinical trial, randomized controlled trial, interventional study.

label: MedicalTrialDesign
comment: Design models for medical trials. Enumerated type.
enriched_comment: An enumeration of design models for medical trials. Also called clinical trial design, trial methodology, study architecture. Examples: "RandomizedControlledTrial", "SingleBlindTrial", "DoubleBlindTrial", "CrossoverTrial".
embedding_text: MedicalTrialDesign (Thing > Intangible > Enumeration > MedicalEnumeration): An enumeration of design models for medical trials. Also called clinical trial design, trial methodology, study architecture.

label: MedicalWebPage
comment: A web page that provides medical information.
enriched_comment: A web page that specifically provides medical information. Also called health information page, clinical webpage, medical content page. Examples: a page describing a disease, a page explaining a medical procedure, a doctor's profile page. Distinct from WebPage, which is a broader category for any web document.
embedding_text: MedicalWebPage (Thing > CreativeWork > WebPage): A web page that specifically provides medical information. Also called health information page, clinical webpage, medical content page.

label: MedicineSystem
comment: Systems of medical practice.
enriched_comment: An enumeration representing different systems of medical practice. Also called healthcare system, medical tradition, healing approach. Examples: "WesternConventional", "Ayurvedic", "TraditionalChineseMedicine", "Homeopathic".
embedding_text: MedicineSystem (Thing > Intangible > Enumeration > MedicalEnumeration): An enumeration representing different systems of medical practice. Also called healthcare system, medical tradition, healing approach.

label: MeetingRoom
comment: A meeting room, conference room, or conference hall is a room provided for singular events such as business conferences and meetings (source: Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia, see http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conference_hall ). See also the dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations .
enriched_comment: A room within an accommodation, such as a hotel, provided for singular events like business conferences and meetings. Also called conference room, conference hall, boardroom, event space. Examples: a hotel's grand ballroom, a corporate meeting room, a small seminar room. Distinct from Room, which is a general category for any room.
embedding_text: MeetingRoom (Thing > Place > Accommodation > Room): A room within an accommodation, such as a hotel, provided for singular events like business conferences and meetings. Also called conference room, conference hall, boardroom, event space.

label: MemberProgram
comment: A MemberProgram defines a loyalty (or membership) program that provides its members with certain benefits, for example better pricing, free shipping or returns, or the ability to earn loyalty points. Member programs may have multiple tiers, for example silver and gold members, each with different benefits.
enriched_comment: An intangible loyalty or membership program that offers specific benefits to its members. Also called loyalty program, membership scheme, rewards program. Examples: an airline frequent flyer program, a supermarket loyalty card, a gym membership.
embedding_text: MemberProgram (Thing > Intangible): An intangible loyalty or membership program that offers specific benefits to its members. Also called loyalty program, membership scheme, rewards program.

label: MemberProgramTier
comment: A MemberProgramTier specifies a tier under a loyalty (member) program, for example "gold".
enriched_comment: An intangible representing a specific tier within a loyalty or membership program. Also called membership level, loyalty tier, program status. Examples: "Gold Member", "Platinum Tier", "Basic Membership Level".
embedding_text: MemberProgramTier (Thing > Intangible): An intangible representing a specific tier within a loyalty or membership program. Also called membership level, loyalty tier, program status.

label: MensClothingStore
comment: A men's clothing store.
enriched_comment: A local business that is a store specializing in men's clothing. Also called men's apparel shop, menswear store, gentlemen's outfitter. Examples: "Brooks Brothers", "Men's Wearhouse", a local boutique for men. Distinct from ClothingStore, which is a broader category.
embedding_text: MensClothingStore (Thing > Organization > LocalBusiness > Store): A local business that is a store specializing in men's clothing. Also called men's apparel shop, menswear store, gentlemen's outfitter.

label: Menu
comment: A structured representation of food or drink items available from a FoodEstablishment.
enriched_comment: A creative work that is a structured representation of food or drink items available from a food establishment. Also called restaurant menu, food list, beverage list. Examples: a dinner menu, a wine list, a dessert menu, a cafe menu.
embedding_text: Menu (Thing > CreativeWork): A creative work that is a structured representation of food or drink items available from a food establishment. Also called restaurant menu, food list, beverage list.

label: MenuItem
comment: A food or drink item listed in a menu or menu section.
enriched_comment: An intangible representing a single food or drink item listed within a menu or menu section. Also called menu item, dish, beverage. Examples: "Spaghetti Carbonara", "Caesar Salad", "Coca-Cola", "Chocolate Lava Cake". Distinct from Menu, which is the entire list.
embedding_text: MenuItem (Thing > Intangible): An intangible representing a single food or drink item listed within a menu or menu section. Also called menu item, dish, beverage.

label: MenuSection
comment: A sub-grouping of food or drink items in a menu. E.g. courses (such as 'Dinner', 'Breakfast', etc.), specific type of dishes (such as 'Meat', 'Vegan', 'Drinks', etc.), or some other classification made by the menu provider.
enriched_comment: A creative work that is a sub-grouping of food or drink items within a menu. Also called menu category, food section, course. Examples: "Appetizers", "Main Courses", "Desserts", "Drinks", "Vegan Options". Distinct from Menu, which is the entire list.
embedding_text: MenuSection (Thing > CreativeWork): A creative work that is a sub-grouping of food or drink items within a menu. Also called menu category, food section, course.

label: MerchantReturnEnumeration
comment: Enumerates several kinds of product return policies.
enriched_comment: An enumeration of various kinds of product return policies offered by merchants. Also called return policy type, refund option, merchandise return category. Examples: "NoReturns", "FreeReturns", "ReturnsWithFee", "ExchangeOnly".
embedding_text: MerchantReturnEnumeration (Thing > Intangible > Enumeration): An enumeration of various kinds of product return policies offered by merchants. Also called return policy type, refund option, merchandise return category.

label: MerchantReturnPolicy
comment: A MerchantReturnPolicy provides information about product return policies associated with an [[Organization]], [[Product]], or [[Offer]].
enriched_comment: An intangible providing information about product return policies associated with an organization, product, or offer. Also called return policy, refund policy, merchandise return terms. Examples: "30-day return policy", "final sale policy", "return policy for electronics".
embedding_text: MerchantReturnPolicy (Thing > Intangible): An intangible providing information about product return policies associated with an organization, product, or offer. Also called return policy, refund policy, merchandise return terms.

label: MerchantReturnPolicySeasonalOverride
comment: A seasonal override of a return policy, for example used for holidays.
enriched_comment: An intangible representing a temporary, seasonal modification to a standard merchant return policy. Also called holiday return policy, seasonal return exception, extended return period. Examples: "extended holiday return window", "special return policy for Black Friday purchases".
embedding_text: MerchantReturnPolicySeasonalOverride (Thing > Intangible): An intangible representing a temporary, seasonal modification to a standard merchant return policy. Also called holiday return policy, seasonal return exception, extended return period.

label: Message
comment: A single message from a sender to one or more organizations or people.
enriched_comment: A creative work representing a single communication from a sender to one or more recipients. Also called communication, dispatch, note, email. Examples: an email, a text message, a direct message on social media, a voicemail.
embedding_text: Message (Thing > CreativeWork): A creative work representing a single communication from a sender to one or more recipients. Also called communication, dispatch, note, email.

label: MiddleSchool
comment: A middle school (typically for children aged around 11-14, although this varies somewhat).
enriched_comment: An educational organization that is a civic structure, typically for children aged around 11-14. Also called junior high school, intermediate school, secondary school (early years). Examples: "Springfield Middle School", "Northwood Junior High", "Acme Intermediate". Distinct from HighSchool, which serves older students.
embedding_text: MiddleSchool (Thing > Place > CivicStructure > EducationalOrganization): An educational organization that is a civic structure, typically for children aged around 11-14. Also called junior high school, intermediate school, secondary school (early years).

label: MobileApplication
comment: A software application designed specifically to work well on a mobile device such as a telephone.
enriched_comment: A software application designed specifically to function effectively on a mobile device. Also called mobile app, smartphone application, tablet app. Examples: "WhatsApp", "Instagram", "Google Maps app", a banking app. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is a broader category for any software.
embedding_text: MobileApplication (Thing > CreativeWork > SoftwareApplication): A software application designed specifically to function effectively on a mobile device. Also called mobile app, smartphone application, tablet app.

label: MobilePhoneStore
comment: A store that sells mobile phones and related accessories.
enriched_comment: A local business that is a store specializing in the sale of mobile phones and related accessories. Also called cell phone shop, smartphone retailer, wireless store. Examples: "Verizon Store", "Apple Store", a local mobile phone dealer. Distinct from ElectronicsStore, which sells a wider range of electronic goods.
embedding_text: MobilePhoneStore (Thing > Organization > LocalBusiness > Store): A local business that is a store specializing in the sale of mobile phones and related accessories. Also called cell phone shop, smartphone retailer, wireless store.

label: MolecularEntity
comment: Any constitutionally or isotopically distinct atom, molecule, ion, ion pair, radical, radical ion, complex, conformer etc., identifiable as a separately distinguishable entity.
enriched_comment: A biochemical entity representing any constitutionally or isotopically distinct atom, molecule, ion, or complex identifiable as a separate entity. Also called chemical entity, molecule, ion, compound. Examples: "water (H2O)", "glucose", "sodium ion (Na+)", "DNA". Distinct from BioChemEntity, which is a broader category for biological and chemical entities.
embedding_text: MolecularEntity (Thing > BioChemEntity): A biochemical entity representing any constitutionally or isotopically distinct atom, molecule, ion, or complex identifiable as a separate entity. Also called chemical entity, molecule, ion, compound.

label: MonetaryAmount
comment: A monetary value or range. This type can be used to describe an amount of money such as $50 USD, or a range as in describing a bank account being suitable for a balance between £1,000 and £1,000,000 GBP, or the value of a salary, etc. It is recommended to use [[PriceSpecification]] Types to describe the price of an Offer, Invoice, etc.
enriched_comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.
embedding_text: MonetaryAmount (Thing > Intangible > StructuredValue): A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount.

label: MonetaryAmountDistribution
comment: A statistical distribution of monetary amounts.
enriched_comment: A quantitative value distribution representing a statistical distribution of monetary amounts. Also called money distribution, financial range, income distribution. Examples: "average salary range", "distribution of asset values", "price range for a product category".
embedding_text: MonetaryAmountDistribution (Thing > Intangible > StructuredValue > QuantitativeValueDistribution): A quantitative value distribution representing a statistical distribution of monetary amounts. Also called money distribution, financial range, income distribution.

label: MonetaryGrant
comment: A monetary grant.
enriched_comment: An intangible grant that provides a sum of money. Also called financial grant, money award, cash donation. Examples: a research grant, a scholarship, a government subsidy. Distinct from Grant, which can be non-monetary.
embedding_text: MonetaryGrant (Thing > Intangible > Grant): An intangible grant that provides a sum of money. Also called financial grant, money award, cash donation.

label: MoneyTransfer
comment: The act of transferring money from one place to another place. This may occur electronically or physically.
enriched_comment: The action of transferring money from one place to another, either electronically or physically. Also called fund transfer, wire transfer, remittance, cash transfer. Examples: sending money via a banking app, wiring funds internationally, handing over cash. Distinct from TransferAction, which is a broader category for moving any object.
embedding_text: MoneyTransfer (Thing > Action > TransferAction): The action of transferring money from one place to another, either electronically or physically. Also called fund transfer, wire transfer, remittance, cash transfer.

label: MortgageLoan
comment: A loan in which property or real estate is used as collateral. (A loan securitized against some real estate.)
enriched_comment: A loan or credit product where property or real estate is used as collateral. Also called home loan, property loan, real estate financing. Examples: a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage, a variable-rate home loan, a commercial property mortgage. Distinct from LoanOrCredit, which is a general loan and not necessarily secured by real estate.
embedding_text: MortgageLoan (Thing > Intangible > Service > FinancialProduct > LoanOrCredit): A loan or credit product where property or real estate is used as collateral. Also called home loan, property loan, real estate financing.

label: Mosque
comment: A mosque.
enriched_comment: A civic structure that is a place of worship for Muslims. Also called masjid, Islamic house of worship, Islamic center. Examples: "Blue Mosque", "Faisal Mosque", a local community mosque. Distinct from PlaceOfWorship, which is a broader category.
embedding_text: Mosque (Thing > Place > CivicStructure > PlaceOfWorship): A civic structure that is a place of worship for Muslims. Also called masjid, Islamic house of worship, Islamic center.

label: Motel
comment: A motel. See also the dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations .
enriched_comment: A lodging business, typically located along a highway, offering rooms with direct access from a parking area. Also called motor hotel, roadside inn, motor lodge. Examples: "Super 8 Motel", "Motel 6", a local roadside motel. Distinct from Hotel, which is generally a larger, multi-story building with interior corridors.
embedding_text: Motel (Thing > Organization > LocalBusiness > LodgingBusiness): A lodging business, typically located along a highway, offering rooms with direct access from a parking area. Also called motor hotel, roadside inn, motor lodge.

label: Motorcycle
comment: A motorcycle or motorbike is a single-track, two-wheeled motor vehicle.
enriched_comment: A vehicle that is a single-track, two-wheeled motor vehicle. Also called motorbike, two-wheeler, scooter. Examples: a Harley-Davidson, a Honda CBR, a Vespa scooter. Distinct from MotorizedBicycle, which is primarily a bicycle with an assisting motor.
embedding_text: Motorcycle (Thing > Product > Vehicle): A vehicle that is a single-track, two-wheeled motor vehicle. Also called motorbike, two-wheeler, scooter.

label: MotorcycleDealer
comment: A motorcycle dealer.
enriched_comment: An automotive business that sells motorcycles. Also called motorbike dealership, motorcycle retailer, bike shop. Examples: "Harley-Davidson Dealership", "Honda Powersports", a local motorcycle store. Distinct from CarDealer, which sells automobiles.
embedding_text: MotorcycleDealer (Thing > Organization > LocalBusiness > AutomotiveBusiness): An automotive business that sells motorcycles. Also called motorbike dealership, motorcycle retailer, bike shop.

label: MotorcycleRepair
comment: A motorcycle repair shop.
enriched_comment: An automotive business that provides repair services for motorcycles. Also called motorbike repair shop, motorcycle service center, bike mechanic. Examples: "Joe's Motorcycle Repair", "Custom Bike Service", a local mechanic specializing in motorcycles. Distinct from AutoRepair, which focuses on cars.
embedding_text: MotorcycleRepair (Thing > Organization > LocalBusiness > AutomotiveBusiness): An automotive business that provides repair services for motorcycles. Also called motorbike repair shop, motorcycle service center, bike mechanic.

label: MotorizedBicycle
comment: A motorized bicycle is a bicycle with an attached motor used to power the vehicle, or to assist with pedaling.
enriched_comment: A vehicle that is primarily a bicycle equipped with an attached motor for power or assistance. Also called e-bike, electric bicycle, moped (older sense). Examples: a pedal-assist electric bicycle, a bicycle with a small gas engine kit. Distinct from Motorcycle, which is designed from the ground up as a motor vehicle.
embedding_text: MotorizedBicycle (Thing > Product > Vehicle): A vehicle that is primarily a bicycle equipped with an attached motor for power or assistance. Also called e-bike, electric bicycle, moped (older sense).

label: Mountain
comment: A mountain, like Mount Whitney or Mount Everest.
enriched_comment: A landform that is a large natural elevation of the earth's surface, typically rising to a summit. Also called peak, mount, range. Examples: "Mount Everest", "Mount Fuji", "Rocky Mountains", "Mount Kilimanjaro". Distinct from Landform, which is a broader category for natural geographical features.
embedding_text: Mountain (Thing > Place > Landform): A landform that is a large natural elevation of the earth's surface, typically rising to a summit. Also called peak, mount, range.

label: MoveAction
comment:
The act of an agent relocating to a place.

Related actions:

* [[TransferAction]]: Unlike TransferAction, the subject of the move is a living Person or Organization rather than an inanimate object.
enriched_comment: An action where a living agent, such as a person or organization, relocates to a different place. Also called relocate, transfer residence, change location. Examples: moving to a new city, a company relocating its headquarters, a person walking to another room. Distinct from TransferAction, where the subject being moved is an inanimate object.
embedding_text: MoveAction (Thing > Action): An action where a living agent, such as a person or organization, relocates to a different place. Also called relocate, transfer residence, change location.

label: Movie
comment: A movie.
enriched_comment: A creative work that is a motion picture film. Also called film, motion picture, cinema. Examples: "The Shawshank Redemption", "Avatar", "Parasite", "Casablanca". Distinct from TVSeries, which is a collection of episodes.
embedding_text: Movie (Thing > CreativeWork): A creative work that is a motion picture film. Also called film, motion picture, cinema.

label: MovieClip
comment: A short segment/part of a movie.
enriched_comment: A MovieClip, as a CreativeWork Clip, is a short segment or part of a movie. Also called film clip, video clip, movie segment, film segment. Examples: a movie trailer, a deleted scene, a blooper reel, a short excerpt used in a review. Distinct from MovieSeries, which is a collection of related films.
embedding_text: MovieClip (Thing > CreativeWork > Clip): A MovieClip, as a CreativeWork Clip, is a short segment or part of a movie. Also called film clip, video clip, movie segment, film segment.

label: MovieRentalStore
comment: A movie rental store.
enriched_comment: A MovieRentalStore is a local business that offers movies for rent. Also called video rental store, film rental shop, DVD rental store. Examples: Blockbuster (historical), local video rental shop, Redbox kiosk. Distinct from MovieTheater, which is a venue for viewing movies.
embedding_text: MovieRentalStore (Thing > Organization > LocalBusiness > Store): A MovieRentalStore is a local business that offers movies for rent. Also called video rental store, film rental shop, DVD rental store.

label: MovieSeries
comment: A series of movies. Included movies can be indicated with the hasPart property.
enriched_comment: A MovieSeries, as a CreativeWorkSeries, is a collection of related movies. Also called film series, movie franchise, film saga. Examples: The Lord of the Rings trilogy, the James Bond film series, the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Distinct from MovieClip, which is a short segment of a single movie.
embedding_text: MovieSeries (Thing > CreativeWork > CreativeWorkSeries): A MovieSeries, as a CreativeWorkSeries, is a collection of related movies. Also called film series, movie franchise, film saga.

label: MovieTheater
comment: A movie theater.
enriched_comment: A MovieTheater is a civic structure designed for public viewing of movies. Also called cinema, picture house, movie house. Examples: AMC Theatres, local independent cinema, drive-in movie theater. Distinct from MovieRentalStore, which is a business for renting movies.
embedding_text: MovieTheater (Thing > Place > CivicStructure): A MovieTheater is a civic structure designed for public viewing of movies. Also called cinema, picture house, movie house.

label: MovingCompany
comment: A moving company.
enriched_comment: A MovingCompany is a local business that provides services for relocating belongings. Also called relocation service, removal company, movers. Examples: U-Haul, Two Men and a Truck, local moving service. Distinct from HomeAndConstructionBusiness, which is a broader category for home-related services.
embedding_text: MovingCompany (Thing > Organization > LocalBusiness > HomeAndConstructionBusiness): A MovingCompany is a local business that provides services for relocating belongings. Also called relocation service, removal company, movers.

label: Muscle
comment: A muscle is an anatomical structure consisting of a contractile form of tissue that animals use to effect movement.
enriched_comment: A Muscle, as an AnatomicalStructure, is a contractile tissue that animals use to effect movement. Also called muscular tissue, skeletal muscle, smooth muscle. Examples: biceps, quadriceps, diaphragm, heart muscle. Distinct from Nerve, which transmits electrochemical impulses.
embedding_text: Muscle (Thing > MedicalEntity > AnatomicalStructure): A Muscle, as an AnatomicalStructure, is a contractile tissue that animals use to effect movement. Also called muscular tissue, skeletal muscle, smooth muscle.

label: Museum
comment: A museum.
enriched_comment: A Museum is a civic structure dedicated to preserving and exhibiting artifacts, art, or scientific specimens. Also called gallery, exhibition hall, cultural institution. Examples: The Louvre, Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History, local art gallery. Distinct from Library, which primarily lends books and media.
embedding_text: Museum (Thing > Place > CivicStructure): A Museum is a civic structure dedicated to preserving and exhibiting artifacts, art, or scientific specimens. Also called gallery, exhibition hall, cultural institution.

label: MusicAlbum
comment: A collection of music tracks.
enriched_comment: A MusicAlbum, as a MusicPlaylist, is a collection of music tracks released together. Also called album, record album, studio album. Examples: 'Thriller' by Michael Jackson, 'Abbey Road' by The Beatles, a compilation album. Distinct from MusicRecording, which is usually a single song.
embedding_text: MusicAlbum (Thing > CreativeWork > MusicPlaylist): A MusicAlbum, as a MusicPlaylist, is a collection of music tracks released together. Also called album, record album, studio album.

label: MusicAlbumProductionType
comment: Classification of the album by its type of content: soundtrack, live album, studio album, etc.
enriched_comment: MusicAlbumProductionType is an enumeration classifying a music album by its content type. Also called album type, production category. Examples: StudioAlbum, LiveAlbum, Soundtrack, CompilationAlbum. Distinct from MusicAlbumReleaseType, which describes the release format.
embedding_text: MusicAlbumProductionType (Thing > Intangible > Enumeration): MusicAlbumProductionType is an enumeration classifying a music album by its content type. Also called album type, production category.

label: MusicAlbumReleaseType

label: Number
comment:
Data type: Number.

Usage guidelines:

* Use values from 0123456789 (Unicode 'DIGIT ZERO' (U+0030) to 'DIGIT NINE' (U+0039)) rather than superficially similar Unicode symbols.
* Use '.' (Unicode 'FULL STOP' (U+002E)) rather than ',' to indicate a decimal point. Avoid using these symbols as a readability separator.
enriched_comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.
embedding_text: Number: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit.

label: Observation
comment: Instances of the class [[Observation]] are used to specify observations about an entity at a particular time. The principal properties of an [[Observation]] are [[observationAbout]], [[measuredProperty]], [[statType]], [[value] and [[observationDate]] and [[measuredProperty]]. Some but not all Observations represent a [[QuantitativeValue]]. Quantitative observations can be about a [[StatisticalVariable]], which is an abstract specification about which we can make observations that are grounded at a particular location and time. Observations can also encode a subset of simple RDF-like statements (its observationAbout, a StatisticalVariable, defining the measuredPoperty; its observationAbout property indicating the entity the statement is about, and [[value]] ) In the context of a quantitative knowledge graph, typical properties could include [[measuredProperty]], [[observationAbout]], [[observationDate]], [[value]], [[unitCode]], [[unitText]], [[measurementMethod]].
enriched_comment: An Observation is an intangible entity used to specify observations about an entity at a particular time, often quantitative. Also called measurement, data point, recorded value. Examples: a temperature reading, a stock price at a specific time, a survey response. Distinct from QuantitativeValue, which is a specific type of observation with a numerical value and unit.
embedding_text: Observation (Thing > Intangible): An Observation is an intangible entity used to specify observations about an entity at a particular time, often quantitative. Also called measurement, data point, recorded value.

label: Offer
comment:
An offer to transfer some rights to an item or to provide a service — for example, an offer to sell tickets to an event, to rent the DVD of a movie, to stream a TV show over the internet, to repair a motorcycle, or to loan a book.

Note: As the [[businessFunction]] property, which identifies the form of offer (e.g. sell, lease, repair, dispose), defaults to http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Sell; an Offer without a defined businessFunction value can be assumed to be an offer to sell.

For [GTIN](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/technical/idkeys/gtin)-related fields, see [Check Digit calculator](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/support/check_digit_calculator) and [validation guide](http://www.gs1us.org/resources/standards/gtin-validation-guide) from [GS1](http://www.gs1.org/).
enriched_comment: An Offer is an intangible entity representing a proposal to transfer rights to an item or provide a service. Also called proposal, deal, listing. Examples: an offer to sell a product, a rental agreement for an apartment, a service quote for car repair. Distinct from Order, which is a confirmation of an accepted offer.
embedding_text: Offer (Thing > Intangible): An Offer is an intangible entity representing a proposal to transfer rights to an item or provide a service. Also called proposal, deal, listing.

Examples: an online store's product categories, a printed catalog of items for sale, a menu of services. Distinct from ItemList, which is a general list of items.
embedding_text: OfferCatalog (Thing > Intangible > ItemList): An OfferCatalog is an ItemList containing related Offers and/or further OfferCatalogs from the same provider. Also called product catalog, service catalog, sales brochure.

embedding_text: OfferForLease (Thing > Intangible > Offer): An OfferForLease, as an Offer, represents a proposal to lease out something. Also called lease offer, rental offer, tenancy proposal.

label: OfferShippingDetails

A different one for all France. Multiple of these entities can be used to represent different shipping costs and delivery times. Two entities that are identical but differ in rate and time: E.g. Cheaper and slower: $5 in 5-7 days or Fast and expensive: $15 in 1-2 days.

label: OrderStatus

enriched_comment: OrderStatus is an enumeration for the status values of an Order. Also called order state, delivery status, fulfillment status. Examples: OrderProcessing, OrderDelivered, OrderCancelled, OrderProblem. Distinct from PaymentStatusType, which describes the payment's state.
embedding_text: OrderStatus (Thing > Intangible > Enumeration > StatusEnumeration): OrderStatus is an enumeration for the status values of an Order. Also called order state, delivery status, fulfillment status.

label: Organization
comment: An organization such as a school, NGO, corporation, club, etc.
enriched_comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.
embedding_text: Organization (Thing): An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association.

label: OrganizationRole
comment: A subclass of Role used to describe roles within organizations.
enriched_comment: An OrganizationRole, as a Role, describes a specific function or position within an organization. Also called organizational position, corporate role, job title. Examples: CEO, Marketing Manager, Board Member, Volunteer Coordinator. Distinct from Role, which is a broader category for any role.
embedding_text: OrganizationRole (Thing > Intangible > Role): An OrganizationRole, as a Role, describes a specific function or position within an organization. Also called organizational position, corporate role, job title.

label: OrganizeAction
comment: The act of manipulating/administering/supervising/controlling one or more objects.
enriched_comment: An OrganizeAction, as an Action, is the act of manipulating, administering, supervising, or controlling one or more objects. Also called arrange, manage, coordinate. Examples: organizing a conference, managing a project, arranging files on a computer. Distinct from CreateAction, which focuses on producing something new.
embedding_text: OrganizeAction (Thing > Action): An OrganizeAction, as an Action, is the act of manipulating, administering, supervising, or controlling one or more objects. Also called arrange, manage, coordinate.

label: OutletStore
comment: An outlet store.
enriched_comment: An OutletStore is a local business that sells goods, often at reduced prices, directly from a manufacturer or retailer. Also called factory outlet, discount store, clearance store. Examples: a Nike outlet, a designer brand outlet, a retail chain's clearance center. Distinct from DepartmentStore, which sells a wide range of goods at regular prices.
embedding_text: OutletStore (Thing > Organization > LocalBusiness > Store): An OutletStore is a local business that sells goods, often at reduced prices, directly from a manufacturer or retailer. Also called factory outlet, discount store, clearance store.

label: OwnershipInfo
comment: A structured value providing information about when a certain organization or person owned a certain product.
enriched_comment: OwnershipInfo, as a StructuredValue, provides information about when a certain organization or person owned a product. Also called ownership details, possession record, property history. Examples: 'Owned by John Doe from 2010-2015', 'Acquired by Company X on Jan 1, 2020'. Distinct from Offer, which is about a potential transaction.
embedding_text: OwnershipInfo (Thing > Intangible > StructuredValue): OwnershipInfo, as a StructuredValue, provides information about when a certain organization or person owned a product. Also called ownership details, possession record, property history.

label: PaintAction
comment: The act of producing a painting, typically with paint and canvas as instruments.
enriched_comment: A PaintAction, as a CreateAction, is the act of producing a painting, typically using paint and canvas. Also called painting, art creation, artistic rendering. Examples: painting a portrait, creating a landscape artwork, applying paint to a wall. Distinct from DrawAction, which typically involves lines and pencils.
embedding_text: PaintAction (Thing > Action > CreateAction): A PaintAction, as a CreateAction, is the act of producing a painting, typically using paint and canvas. Also called painting, art creation, artistic rendering.

label: Painting
comment: A painting.
enriched_comment: A Painting, as a CreativeWork, is an artwork created by applying paint to a surface. Also called artwork, canvas, oil painting. Examples: Leonardo da Vinci's 'Mona Lisa', a watercolor landscape, an abstract acrylic painting. Distinct from Photograph, which is an image captured by a camera.
embedding_text: Painting (Thing > CreativeWork): A Painting, as a CreativeWork, is an artwork created by applying paint to a surface. Also called artwork, canvas, oil painting.

label: PalliativeProcedure
comment: A medical procedure intended primarily for palliative purposes, aimed at relieving the symptoms of an underlying health condition.
enriched_comment: A PalliativeProcedure, as a MedicalProcedure, is a medical procedure primarily intended to relieve symptoms of an underlying health condition. Also called palliative treatment, symptom management procedure, comfort care procedure. Examples: pain management surgery, stent placement to relieve obstruction, nerve block for chronic pain. Distinct from DiagnosticProcedure, which aims to identify a condition.
embedding_text: PalliativeProcedure (Thing > MedicalEntity > MedicalProcedure): A PalliativeProcedure, as a MedicalProcedure, is a medical procedure primarily intended to relieve symptoms of an underlying health condition. Also called palliative treatment, symptom management procedure, comfort care procedure.

label: ParcelDelivery
comment: The delivery of a parcel either via the postal service or a commercial service.
enriched_comment: A ParcelDelivery is an intangible entity representing the delivery of a parcel via postal or commercial service. Also called package delivery, shipment, courier service. Examples: a UPS package delivery, a letter sent via postal service, an Amazon shipment. Distinct from Order, which is the transaction itself.
embedding_text: ParcelDelivery (Thing > Intangible): A ParcelDelivery is an intangible entity representing the delivery of a parcel via postal or commercial service. Also called package delivery, shipment, courier service.

label: ParentAudience
comment: A set of characteristics describing parents, who can be interested in viewing some content.
enriched_comment: A ParentAudience, as a PeopleAudience, describes characteristics of parents who might be interested in certain content. Also called parental demographic, parent group, family audience. Examples: 'parents of young children', 'parents of teenagers', 'expectant parents'. Distinct from PeopleAudience, which is a broader category for any group of people.
embedding_text: ParentAudience (Thing > Intangible > Audience > PeopleAudience): A ParentAudience, as a PeopleAudience, describes characteristics of parents who might be interested in certain content. Also called parental demographic, parent group, family audience.

label: Park
comment: A park.
enriched_comment: A Park is a civic structure or area of natural, semi-natural, or planted space set aside for human recreation or protection of wildlife. Also called public park, green space, recreation area. Examples: Central Park in New York City, a local neighborhood park, a national park. Distinct from Garden, which is typically smaller and privately owned.
embedding_text: Park (Thing > Place > CivicStructure): A Park is a civic structure or area of natural, semi-natural, or planted space set aside for human recreation or protection of wildlife. Also called public park, green space, recreation area.

label: ParkingFacility
comment: A parking lot or other parking facility.
enriched_comment: A ParkingFacility is a civic structure providing space for parking vehicles. Also called parking lot, parking garage, car park. Examples: a multi-story parking garage, a supermarket parking lot, a valet parking service. Distinct from Road, which is for vehicle travel.
embedding_text: ParkingFacility (Thing > Place > CivicStructure): A ParkingFacility is a civic structure providing space for parking vehicles. Also called parking lot, parking garage, car park.

label: PathologyTest
comment: A medical test performed by a laboratory that typically involves examination of a tissue sample by a pathologist.
enriched_comment: A PathologyTest, as a MedicalTest, is a medical test performed by a laboratory, typically involving examination of a tissue sample by a pathologist. Also called biopsy, tissue analysis, lab pathology. Examples: a biopsy for cancer diagnosis, a blood smear analysis, a genetic test on a tissue sample. Distinct from BloodTest, which specifically analyzes blood.
embedding_text: PathologyTest (Thing > MedicalEntity > MedicalTest): A PathologyTest, as a MedicalTest, is a medical test performed by a laboratory, typically involving examination of a tissue sample by a pathologist. Also called biopsy, tissue analysis, lab pathology.

label: Patient
comment: A patient is any person recipient of health care services.
enriched_comment: A Patient, as a MedicalAudience, is any person receiving health care services. Also called healthcare recipient, medical client, care receiver. Examples: a person visiting a doctor for a check-up, someone undergoing surgery, a person receiving therapy. Distinct from Physician, who provides medical care.
embedding_text: Patient (Thing > Intangible > Audience > MedicalAudience): A Patient, as a MedicalAudience, is any person receiving health care services. Also called healthcare recipient, medical client, care receiver.

label: PawnShop
comment: A shop that will buy, or lend money against the security of, personal possessions.
enriched_comment: A PawnShop is a local business that lends money against personal possessions or buys them outright. Also called pawnbroker, second-hand store (if buying). Examples: a local pawn shop, a jewelry and loan store. Distinct from RetailStore, which primarily sells new goods.
embedding_text: PawnShop (Thing > Organization > LocalBusiness > Store): A PawnShop is a local business that lends money against personal possessions or buys them outright. Also called pawnbroker, second-hand store (if buying).

label: PayAction
comment: An agent pays a price to a participant.
enriched_comment: A PayAction, as a TradeAction, is an action where an agent transfers a price to a participant. Also called make payment, remit funds, settle bill. Examples: paying for groceries, paying rent, settling a debt. Distinct from OrderAction, which is about requesting goods or services.
embedding_text: PayAction (Thing > Action > TradeAction): A PayAction, as a TradeAction, is an action where an agent transfers a price to a participant. Also called make payment, remit funds, settle bill.

label: PaymentCard
comment: A payment method using a credit, debit, store or other card to associate the payment with an account.
enriched_comment: A PaymentCard, as a FinancialProduct, is a payment method using a credit, debit, store, or other card. Also called credit card, debit card, store card. Examples: Visa credit card, Mastercard debit card, a store loyalty card with payment function. Distinct from BankAccount, which is a financial account.
embedding_text: PaymentCard (Thing > Intangible > Service > FinancialProduct): A PaymentCard, as a FinancialProduct, is a payment method using a credit, debit, store, or other card. Also called credit card, debit card, store card.

label: PaymentChargeSpecification
comment: The costs of settling the payment using a particular payment method.
enriched_comment: A PaymentChargeSpecification, as a PriceSpecification, describes the costs of settling a payment using a particular method. Also called payment fee, transaction charge, processing fee. Examples: '3% credit card processing fee', 'bank transfer fee of $5', 'no charge for cash payments'. Distinct from PriceSpecification, which is a general price description.
embedding_text: PaymentChargeSpecification (Thing > Intangible > StructuredValue > PriceSpecification): A PaymentChargeSpecification, as a PriceSpecification, describes the costs of settling a payment using a particular method. Also called payment fee, transaction charge, processing fee.

label: PaymentMethod
comment:
A payment method is a standardized procedure for transferring the monetary amount for a purchase. Payment methods are characterized by the legal and technical structures used, and by the organization or group carrying out the transaction. The following legacy values should be accepted: 

* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#ByBankTransferInAdvance
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#ByInvoice
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Cash
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#CheckInAdvance
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#COD
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DirectDebit
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#GoogleCheckout
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#PayPal
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#PaySwarm

Structured values, or [UNCE payment means](https://vocabulary.uncefact.org/PaymentMeans) are recommended or for newer annotations.
enriched_comment: A PaymentMethod is an intangible entity representing a standardized procedure for transferring monetary amounts for a purchase. Also called payment option, mode of payment, transaction method. Examples: Cash, CreditCard, BankTransfer, PayPal. Distinct from PaymentMethodType, which is a generic classification.
embedding_text: PaymentMethod (Thing > Intangible): A PaymentMethod is an intangible entity representing a standardized procedure for transferring monetary amounts for a purchase. Also called payment option, mode of payment, transaction method.

label: PaymentMethodType
comment: The type of payment method, only for generic payment types, specific forms of payments, like card payment should be expressed using subclasses of PaymentMethod.
enriched_comment: PaymentMethodType is an enumeration for generic types of payment methods. Also called payment category, payment classification. Examples: CreditCard, DebitCard, BankTransfer, Cash. Distinct from PaymentMethod, which can be a specific instance or a broader concept.
embedding_text: PaymentMethodType (Thing > Intangible > Enumeration): PaymentMethodType is an enumeration for generic types of payment methods. Also called payment category, payment classification.

label: PaymentService
comment: A Service to transfer funds from a person or organization to a beneficiary person or organization.
enriched_comment: A PaymentService, as a FinancialProduct, is a service to transfer funds between persons or organizations. Also called money transfer service, payment processing service, remittance service. Examples: PayPal, Western Union, a bank's wire transfer service. Distinct from BankAccount, which is an account, not a service.
embedding_text: PaymentService (Thing > Intangible > Service > FinancialProduct): A PaymentService, as a FinancialProduct, is a service to transfer funds between persons or organizations. Also called money transfer service, payment processing service, remittance service.

label: PaymentStatusType
comment: A specific payment status. For example, PaymentDue, PaymentComplete, etc.
enriched_comment: PaymentStatusType is an enumeration for specific payment statuses. Also called payment state, transaction status, billing status. Examples: PaymentDue, PaymentComplete, PaymentDeclined, PaymentFailed. Distinct from OrderStatus, which describes the overall order state.
embedding_text: PaymentStatusType (Thing > Intangible > Enumeration > StatusEnumeration): PaymentStatusType is an enumeration for specific payment statuses. Also called payment state, transaction status, billing status.

label: PeopleAudience
comment: A set of characteristics belonging to people, e.g. who compose an item's target audience.
enriched_comment: A PeopleAudience, as an Audience, describes a set of characteristics belonging to people, e.g., who compose an item's target audience. Also called demographic group, target audience, human audience. Examples: 'adults aged 18-35', 'students', 'retirees'. Distinct from Audience, which is a broader category including non-human audiences.
embedding_text: PeopleAudience (Thing > Intangible > Audience): A PeopleAudience, as an Audience, describes a set of characteristics belonging to people, e.g., who compose an item's target audience. Also called demographic group, target audience, human audience.

label: PerformAction
comment: The act of participating in performance arts.
enriched_comment: A PerformAction, as a PlayAction, is the act of participating in performance arts. Also called act, perform, stage. Examples: performing in a play, playing a musical instrument on stage, dancing in a ballet. Distinct from PlayAction, which is a broader category for engaging in recreational activities.
embedding_text: PerformAction (Thing > Action > PlayAction): A PerformAction, as a PlayAction, is the act of participating in performance arts. Also called act, perform, stage.

label: PerformanceRole
comment: A PerformanceRole is a Role that some entity places with regard to a theatrical performance, e.g. in a Movie, TVSeries etc.
enriched_comment: A PerformanceRole, as a Role, is a role an entity plays in a theatrical performance, such as a movie or TV series. Also called acting role, character role, stage role. Examples: 'actor in a film', 'director of a play', 'musician in a concert'. Distinct from OrganizationRole, which is a role within an organization.
embedding_text: PerformanceRole (Thing > Intangible > Role): A PerformanceRole, as a Role, is a role an entity plays in a theatrical performance, such as a movie or TV series. Also called acting role, character role, stage role.

label: PerformingArtsEvent
comment: Live performance Event of the performing arts (music, theatre, dance, acrobatics, spoken word), including performance art and performative sports (e.g. choreographed forms of martial arts, figure skating, competitive ballroom dancing). Note: Use additionalType to differentiate between productions / shows (PerformanceWork, EventSeries), tours (EventSeries), and individual performances.
enriched_comment: A PerformingArtsEvent is an event featuring live performances of arts like music, theatre, dance, or acrobatics. Also called live performance, show, stage event. Examples: a Broadway play, a ballet performance, a circus show, a stand-up comedy act. Distinct from MusicEvent, which is specifically for music.
embedding_text: PerformingArtsEvent (Thing > Event): A PerformingArtsEvent is an event featuring live performances of arts like music, theatre, dance, or acrobatics. Also called live performance, show, stage event.

label: PerformingArtsTheater
comment: A theater or other performing art center.
enriched_comment: A PerformingArtsTheater is a civic structure or venue for performing arts. Also called theater, playhouse, concert hall. Examples: Sydney Opera House, a local community theater, a Broadway theater. Distinct from MovieTheater, which is for film screenings.
embedding_text: PerformingArtsTheater (Thing > Place > CivicStructure): A PerformingArtsTheater is a civic structure or venue for performing arts. Also called theater, playhouse, concert hall.

label: PerformingGroup
comment: A performance group, such as a band, an orchestra, or a circus.
enriched_comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.
embedding_text: PerformingGroup (Thing > Organization): A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group.

label: Periodical
comment: A publication in any medium issued in successive parts bearing numerical or chronological designations and intended to continue indefinitely, such as a magazine, scholarly journal, or newspaper.\n\nSee also [blog post](https://blog.schema.org/2014/09/02/schema-org-support-for-bibliographic-relationships-and-periodicals/).
enriched_comment: A Periodical, as a CreativeWorkSeries, is a publication issued in successive parts with numerical or chronological designations, intended to continue indefinitely. Also called serial publication, magazine, journal. Examples: The New Yorker magazine, a scholarly journal, a daily newspaper. Distinct from Book, which is a single, non-serial publication.
embedding_text: Periodical (Thing > CreativeWork > CreativeWorkSeries): A Periodical, as a CreativeWorkSeries, is a publication issued in successive parts with numerical or chronological designations, intended to continue indefinitely. Also called serial publication, magazine, journal.

label: Permit
comment: A permit issued by an organization, e.g. a parking pass.
enriched_comment: A Permit is an intangible entity representing an official authorization issued by an organization. Also called license, authorization, pass. Examples: a building permit, a parking permit, a fishing license. Distinct from LegalService, which is a service, not the document itself.
embedding_text: Permit (Thing > Intangible): A Permit is an intangible entity representing an official authorization issued by an organization. Also called license, authorization, pass.

label: Person
comment: A person (alive, dead, undead, or fictional).
enriched_comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.
embedding_text: Person (Thing): A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character.

label: PetStore
comment: A pet store.
enriched_comment: A PetStore is a local business that sells pets and pet supplies. Also called pet shop, animal store, pet supply retailer. Examples: PetSmart, a local independent pet shop, an online pet supply store. Distinct from VeterinaryCare, which provides animal medical services.
embedding_text: PetStore (Thing > Organization > LocalBusiness > Store): A PetStore is a local business that sells pets and pet supplies. Also called pet shop, animal store, pet supply retailer.

label: Pharmacy
comment: A pharmacy or drugstore.
enriched_comment: A Pharmacy is a local business that dispenses prescription medications and often sells over-the-counter drugs and health products. Also called drugstore, chemist, apothecary. Examples: CVS Pharmacy, Walgreens, a local independent pharmacy. Distinct from Physician, who provides medical consultations.
embedding_text: Pharmacy (Thing > Organization > LocalBusiness > MedicalBusiness): A Pharmacy is a local business that dispenses prescription medications and often sells over-the-counter drugs and health products. Also called drugstore, chemist, apothecary.

label: Photograph
comment: A photograph.
enriched_comment: A Photograph, as a CreativeWork, is an image captured using a camera. Also called photo, picture, image. Examples: a portrait photograph, a landscape photo, a news photograph. Distinct from Painting, which is created with paint.
embedding_text: Photograph (Thing > CreativeWork): A Photograph, as a CreativeWork, is an image captured using a camera. Also called photo, picture, image.

label: PhotographAction
comment: The act of capturing still images of objects using a camera.
enriched_comment: A PhotographAction, as a CreateAction, is the act of capturing still images of objects using a camera. Also called taking a photo, shooting a picture, photography. Examples: taking a selfie, photographing a landscape, shooting a product for an advertisement. Distinct from RecordAction, which captures moving images or sound.
embedding_text: PhotographAction (Thing > Action > CreateAction): A PhotographAction, as a CreateAction, is the act of capturing still images of objects using a camera. Also called taking a photo, shooting a picture, photography.

label: PhysicalActivity
comment: Any bodily activity that enhances or maintains physical fitness and overall health and wellness. Includes activity that is part of daily living and routine, structured exercise, and exercise prescribed as part of a medical treatment or recovery plan.
enriched_comment: PhysicalActivity, as a LifestyleModification, is any bodily activity that enhances or maintains physical fitness and overall health. Also called exercise, workout, physical exertion. Examples: running, swimming, yoga, weightlifting. Distinct from MedicalTherapy, which is a treatment for a specific condition.
embedding_text: PhysicalActivity (Thing > MedicalEntity > LifestyleModification): PhysicalActivity, as a LifestyleModification, is any bodily activity that enhances or maintains physical fitness and overall health. Also called exercise, workout, physical exertion.

label: PhysicalActivityCategory

enriched_comment: PhysicalActivityCategory is an enumeration for categories of physical activity, organized by physiologic classification. Also called exercise type, activity classification. Examples: AerobicActivity, StrengthTraining, Flexibility. Distinct from PhysicalActivity, which is an instance of an activity.
embedding_text: PhysicalActivityCategory (Thing > Intangible > Enumeration): PhysicalActivityCategory is an enumeration for categories of physical activity, organized by physiologic classification. Also called exercise type, activity classification.

label: PhysicalExam

enriched_comment: A PhysicalExam, as a MedicalEnumeration, is a type of physical examination of a patient performed by a physician. Also called medical check-up, physical assessment, health examination. Examples: general physical, sports physical, pre-employment physical. embedding_text: PhysicalExam (Thing > Intangible > Enumeration > MedicalEnumeration): A PhysicalExam, as a MedicalEnumeration, is a type of physical examination of a patient performed by a physician. Also called medical check-up, physical assessment, health examination.

label: PhysicalTherapy

enriched_comment: PhysicalTherapy, as a MedicalTherapy, is a process of progressive physical care and rehabilitation aimed at improving a health condition. Also called physiotherapy, PT, rehabilitation therapy. Examples: exercises to recover from a knee injury, post-stroke rehabilitation, back pain therapy. embedding_text: PhysicalTherapy (Thing > MedicalEntity > MedicalProcedure > TherapeuticProcedure > MedicalTherapy): PhysicalTherapy, as a MedicalTherapy, is a process of progressive physical care and rehabilitation aimed at improving a health condition. Also called physiotherapy, PT, rehabilitation therapy.

label: Physician
comment: An individual physician or a physician's office considered as a [[MedicalOrganization]].
enriched_comment: A Physician, as a MedicalBusiness, is an individual doctor or a doctor's office considered as a MedicalOrganization. Also called doctor, medical practitioner, medical doctor. Examples: a general practitioner, a specialist physician, a family doctor's clinic. Distinct from Hospital, which is a larger medical facility.
embedding_text: Physician (Thing > Organization > LocalBusiness > MedicalBusiness): A Physician, as a MedicalBusiness, is an individual doctor or a doctor's office considered as a MedicalOrganization. Also called doctor, medical practitioner, medical doctor.

label: PhysiciansOffice

enriched_comment: A PhysiciansOffice, as a Physician, is a doctor's office or clinic where medical consultations and treatments are provided. Also called doctor's clinic, medical office, medical practice. Examples: a family doctor's practice, a specialist's clinic, an urgent care center. embedding_text: PhysiciansOffice (Thing > Organization > LocalBusiness > MedicalBusiness > Physician): A PhysiciansOffice, as a Physician, is a doctor's office or clinic where medical consultations and treatments are provided. Also called doctor's clinic, medical office, medical practice.

label: Place

enriched_comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.
embedding_text: Place (Thing): A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site.

label: PlaceOfWorship
comment: Place of worship, such as a church, synagogue, or mosque.
enriched_comment: A PlaceOfWorship is a civic structure or building used for religious services and spiritual activities. Also called religious building, house of worship, sanctuary. Examples: a church, a synagogue, a mosque, a temple. Distinct from Museum, which is for exhibiting artifacts.
embedding_text: PlaceOfWorship (Thing > Place > CivicStructure): A PlaceOfWorship is a civic structure or building used for religious services and spiritual activities. Also called religious building, house of worship, sanctuary.

label: PlanAction

embedding_text: PlanAction (Thing > Action > OrganizeAction): PlanAction is an OrganizeAction that involves arranging the execution of an event, task, action, reservation, or plan for a future time. Also called scheduling, arranging, pre-arranging.

label: Play
comment: A play is a form of literature, usually consisting of dialogue between characters, intended for theatrical performance rather than just reading. Note: A performance of a Play would be a [[TheaterEvent]] or [[BroadcastEvent]] - the *Play* being the [[workPerformed]].
enriched_comment: A Play is a CreativeWork in the form of literature, primarily consisting of dialogue between characters, intended for theatrical performance. Also called stage play, drama, theatrical work. Examples: "Hamlet", "Death of a Salesman", "Hamilton", "A Streetcar Named Desire". Distinct from TheaterEvent, which is the actual performance of a play.
embedding_text: Play (Thing > CreativeWork): A Play is a CreativeWork in the form of literature, primarily consisting of dialogue between characters, intended for theatrical performance. Also called stage play, drama, theatrical work.

label: PlayAction
comment:
The act of playing/exercising/training/performing for enjoyment, leisure, recreation, competition or exercise.

Related actions:

* [[ListenAction]]: Unlike ListenAction (which is under ConsumeAction), PlayAction refers to performing for an audience or at an event, rather than consuming music.
* [[WatchAction]]: Unlike WatchAction (which is under ConsumeAction), PlayAction refers to showing/displaying for an audience or at an event, rather than consuming visual content.
enriched_comment: PlayAction is an Action involving playing, exercising, training, or performing for enjoyment, leisure, recreation, competition, or physical activity. Also called performing, engaging in recreation, exercising. Examples: playing a sport, performing music on stage, training for a marathon, engaging in a hobby. Distinct from ListenAction, which is consuming music; Distinct from WatchAction, which is consuming visual content.
embedding_text: PlayAction (Thing > Action): PlayAction is an Action involving playing, exercising, training, or performing for enjoyment, leisure, recreation, competition, or physical activity. Also called performing, engaging in recreation, exercising.

label: PlayGameAction
comment: The act of playing a video game.
enriched_comment: PlayGameAction is a ConsumeAction specifically representing the act of playing a video game. Also called gaming, video gaming, playing a digital game. Examples: playing "Minecraft", playing "Fortnite", playing "Chess" online, playing a mobile game. Distinct from PlayAction, which is a broader act of playing or performing.
embedding_text: PlayGameAction (Thing > Action > ConsumeAction): PlayGameAction is a ConsumeAction specifically representing the act of playing a video game. Also called gaming, video gaming, playing a digital game.

label: Playground
comment: A playground.

embedding_text: Playground (Thing > Place > CivicStructure): A Playground is a CivicStructure designed for children's recreational play. Also called play area, recreation ground.

label: Plumber
comment: A plumbing service.
enriched_comment: A Plumber is a HomeAndConstructionBusiness providing plumbing services. Also called plumbing contractor, plumbing service provider. Examples: "Joe's Plumbing", a local plumbing company, an emergency plumber, a commercial plumbing service.
embedding_text: Plumber (Thing > Organization > LocalBusiness > HomeAndConstructionBusiness): A Plumber is a HomeAndConstructionBusiness providing plumbing services. Also called plumbing contractor, plumbing service provider.

label: PodcastEpisode
comment: A single episode of a podcast series.
enriched_comment: A PodcastEpisode is an Episode representing a single installment of a podcast series. Also called podcast installment, audio episode. Examples: "The Daily" episode from 2023-10-26, "Serial" Season 1 Episode 1, a specific episode of "Stuff You Should Know".
embedding_text: PodcastEpisode (Thing > CreativeWork > Episode): A PodcastEpisode is an Episode representing a single installment of a podcast series. Also called podcast installment, audio episode.

label: PodcastSeason
comment: A single season of a podcast. Many podcasts do not break down into separate seasons. In that case, PodcastSeries should be used.

embedding_text: PrependAction (Thing > Action > UpdateAction > AddAction > InsertAction): PrependAction is an InsertAction that involves inserting an object at the beginning of an ordered collection. Also called prefixing, adding to front.

embedding_text: PriceComponentTypeEnumeration (Thing > Intangible > Enumeration): PriceComponentTypeEnumeration is an Enumeration listing different types of price components that collectively form the total price of an offered product. Also called price element type, cost breakdown category.
