enriched_comment: A PriceSpecification is a StructuredValue representing a price or price range, typically used for markup of offers. Also called pricing details, cost specification. Examples: a product's list price, a service's hourly rate, a discount price, a price range for a flight. Distinct from MonetaryAmount, which describes independent amounts of money.
embedding_text: PriceSpecification (Thing > Intangible > StructuredValue): A PriceSpecification is a StructuredValue representing a price or price range, typically used for markup of offers. Also called pricing details, cost specification.

label: PriceTypeEnumeration
comment: Enumerates different price types, for example list price, invoice price, and sale price.
enriched_comment: PriceTypeEnumeration is an Enumeration listing different types of prices, such as list price, invoice price, or sale price. Also called pricing category, cost type. Examples: list price, sale price, invoice price, suggested retail price.
embedding_text: PriceTypeEnumeration (Thing > Intangible > Enumeration): PriceTypeEnumeration is an Enumeration listing different types of prices, such as list price, invoice price, or sale price. Also called pricing category, cost type.

label: Product
comment: Any offered product or service. For example: a pair of shoes; a concert ticket; the rental of a car; a haircut; or an episode of a TV show streamed online.
enriched_comment: A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering. Examples: a pair of shoes, a concert ticket, a car rental service, an episode of a TV show.
embedding_text: Product (Thing): A Product is any offered good or service. Also called item, merchandise, offering.

label: ProductCollection
comment: A set of products (either [[ProductGroup]]s or specific variants) that are listed together e.g. in an [[Offer]].
enriched_comment: A ProductCollection is a Collection of products, either ProductGroups or specific variants, listed together, often within an Offer. Also called product assortment, product bundle, product set. Examples: a collection of books by an author, a bundle of software products, a set of kitchen utensils, a curated selection of wines.
embedding_text: ProductCollection (Thing > CreativeWork > Collection): A ProductCollection is a Collection of products, either ProductGroups or specific variants, listed together, often within an Offer. Also called product assortment, product bundle, product set.

label: ProductGroup
comment: A ProductGroup represents a group of [[Product]]s that vary only in certain well-described ways, such as by [[size]], [[color]], [[material]] etc. While a ProductGroup itself is not directly offered for sale, the various varying products that it represents can be. The ProductGroup serves as a prototype or template, standing in for all of the products who have an [[isVariantOf]] relationship to it. As such, properties (including additional types) can be applied to the ProductGroup to represent characteristics shared by each of the (possibly very many) variants. Properties that reference a ProductGroup are not included in this mechanism; neither are the following specific properties [[variesBy]], [[hasVariant]], [[url]].
enriched_comment: A ProductGroup is a Product representing a group of products that vary only in specific attributes like size, color, or material, serving as a template for its variants. Also called product family, product line, variant group. Examples: a specific model of smartphone available in different colors and storage sizes, a t-shirt design available in various sizes and fabrics, a car model with different trim levels. Distinct from Product, which is a specific variant offered for sale.
embedding_text: ProductGroup (Thing > Product): A ProductGroup is a Product representing a group of products that vary only in specific attributes like size, color, or material, serving as a template for its variants. Also called product family, product line, variant group.

label: ProductModel
comment: A datasheet or vendor specification of a product (in the sense of a prototypical description).
enriched_comment: A ProductModel is a Product representing a datasheet or vendor specification of a prototypical product description. Also called product prototype, product specification, product blueprint. Examples: the technical specifications for a new laptop model, a design document for a car engine, a vendor's product data sheet, a conceptual product design.
embedding_text: ProductModel (Thing > Product): A ProductModel is a Product representing a datasheet or vendor specification of a prototypical product description. Also called product prototype, product specification, product blueprint.

label: ProfessionalService
comment: Original definition: "provider of professional services."\n\nThe general [[ProfessionalService]] type for local businesses was deprecated due to confusion with [[Service]]. For reference, the types that it included were: [[Dentist]], [[AccountingService]], [[Attorney]], [[Notary]], as well as types for several kinds of [[HomeAndConstructionBusiness]]: [[Electrician]], [[GeneralContractor]], [[HousePainter]], [[Locksmith]], [[Plumber]], [[RoofingContractor]]. [[LegalService]] was introduced as a more inclusive supertype of [[Attorney]].
enriched_comment: ProfessionalService is a LocalBusiness type for providers of specialized services. Also called expert service, specialized service. Examples: a legal service, an accounting service, a dental practice, an architectural firm. Distinct from Service, which is a broader concept of an intangible offering.
embedding_text: ProfessionalService (Thing > Organization > LocalBusiness): ProfessionalService is a LocalBusiness type for providers of specialized services. Also called expert service, specialized service.

embedding_text: ProfilePage (Thing > CreativeWork > WebPage): A ProfilePage is a WebPage dedicated to displaying information about a specific entity, such as a person or organization. Also called user profile, personal page, bio page.

label: ProgramMembership

embedding_text: ProgramMembership (Thing > Intangible): ProgramMembership is an Intangible describing participation in loyalty programs, traveler clubs, or purchase clubs. Also called membership, loyalty program enrollment, club membership.

label: Property

label: PropertyValue
comment: A property-value pair, e.g. representing a feature of a product or place. Use the 'name' property for the name of the property. If there is an additional human-readable version of the value, put that into the 'description' property.\n\n Always use specific schema.org properties when a) they exist and b) you can populate them. Using PropertyValue as a substitute will typically not trigger the same effect as using the original, specific property.
enriched_comment: A PropertyValue is a StructuredValue representing a property-value pair, such as a feature of a product or place. Also called feature, attribute value, characteristic. Examples: "color: red", "weight: 5kg", "hasWifi: true", "engineType: V8". Distinct from using specific schema.org properties directly, which is preferred when available.
embedding_text: PropertyValue (Thing > Intangible > StructuredValue): A PropertyValue is a StructuredValue representing a property-value pair, such as a feature of a product or place. Also called feature, attribute value, characteristic.

embedding_text: PropertyValueSpecification (Thing > Intangible): A PropertyValueSpecification is an Intangible defining the specification for a property's value. Also called value constraint, property definition.

label: Protein
comment: Protein is here used in its widest possible definition, as classes of amino acid based molecules. Amyloid-beta Protein in human (UniProt P05067), eukaryota (e.g. an OrthoDB group) or even a single molecule that one can point to are all of type :Protein. A protein can thus be a subclass of another protein, e.g. :Protein as a UniProt record can have multiple isoforms inside it which would also be :Protein. They can be imagined, synthetic, hypothetical or naturally occurring.
enriched_comment: A Protein is a BioChemEntity representing classes of amino acid-based molecules, from single molecules to entire groups. Also called polypeptide, amino acid chain. Examples: Amyloid-beta Protein, hemoglobin, insulin, an enzyme.
embedding_text: Protein (Thing > BioChemEntity): A Protein is a BioChemEntity representing classes of amino acid-based molecules, from single molecules to entire groups. Also called polypeptide, amino acid chain.

label: PublicationIssue
comment: A part of a successively published publication such as a periodical or publication volume, often numbered, usually containing a grouping of works such as articles.\n\nSee also [blog post](https://blog-schema.org/2014/09/02/schema-org-support-for-bibliographic-relationships-and-periodicals/).

Distinct from PublicationVolume, which is a larger grouping of issues.
embedding_text: PublicationIssue (Thing > CreativeWork): A PublicationIssue is a CreativeWork representing a part of a successively published periodical or publication volume, often numbered and containing a grouping of works. Also called journal issue, magazine issue, periodical issue.

label: PublicationVolume

enriched_comment: A PublicationVolume is a CreativeWork representing a part of a successively published periodical or multi-volume work, often numbered and potentially spanning a time period. Also called journal volume, book volume, periodical volume. Examples: "Nature" Volume 500; "Encyclopedia Britannica" Volume 1; a year's collection of a magazine. Distinct from PublicationIssue, which is a smaller, more granular part of a volume.
embedding_text: PublicationVolume (Thing > CreativeWork): A PublicationVolume is a CreativeWork representing a part of a successively published periodical or multi-volume work, often numbered and potentially spanning a time period. Also called journal volume, book volume, periodical volume.

label: ReceiveAction

Related actions:

Also called accepting delivery, getting, obtaining. Examples: receiving a package, getting an email, accepting a file download, taking delivery of a new car. Distinct from SendAction, which is the reciprocal action; Distinct from TakeAction, which implies ownership transfer.

label: ReportageNewsArticle
comment: The [[ReportageNewsArticle]] type is a subtype of [[NewsArticle]] representing news articles which are the result of journalistic news reporting conventions. In practice many news publishers produce a wide variety of article types, many of which might be considered a [[NewsArticle]] but not a [[ReportageNewsArticle]]. For example, opinion pieces, reviews, analysis, sponsored or satirical articles, or articles that combine several of these elements. The [[ReportageNewsArticle]] type is based on a stricter ideal for "news" as a work of journalism, with articles based on factual information either observed or verified by the author, or reported and verified from knowledgeable sources. This often includes perspectives from multiple viewpoints on a particular issue (distinguishing news reports from public relations or propaganda). News reports in the [[ReportageNewsArticle]] sense de-emphasize the opinion of the author, with commentary and value judgements typically expressed elsewhere. A [[ReportageNewsArticle]] which goes deeper into analysis can also be marked with an additional type of [[AnalysisNewsArticle]].
enriched_comment: A ReportageNewsArticle is a NewsArticle representing news articles based on factual journalistic reporting, emphasizing verified information and multiple viewpoints. Also called news report, journalistic article, factual news. Examples: a breaking news story about a political event, an investigative report on a social issue, a factual account of a natural disaster, a report on scientific findings. Distinct from AnalysisNewsArticle, which goes deeper into analysis.
embedding_text: ReportageNewsArticle (Thing > CreativeWork > Article > NewsArticle): A ReportageNewsArticle is a NewsArticle representing news articles based on factual journalistic reporting, emphasizing verified information and multiple viewpoints. Also called news report, journalistic article, factual news.

Also called RSVPing, confirming attendance, declining invitation, responding to invite. Examples: accepting a wedding invitation, declining a party invite, indicating 'maybe' for a meeting.
embedding_text: RsvpAction (Thing > Action > InteractAction > CommunicateAction > InformAction): The act of responding to an event organizer to indicate whether one expects to attend the event. Also called RSVPing, confirming attendance, declining invitation, responding to invite.

label: RsvpResponseType
comment: RsvpResponseType is an enumeration type whose instances represent responding to an RSVP request.
enriched_comment: An enumeration type representing the possible responses to an RSVP request. Also called RSVP status, attendance response, invitation reply type. Examples: RsvpResponseType.Yes, RsvpResponseType.No, RsvpResponseType.MayBe.
embedding_text: RsvpResponseType (Thing > Intangible > Enumeration): An enumeration type representing the possible responses to an RSVP request. Also called RSVP status, attendance response, invitation reply type.

label: RuntimePlatform
comment: Specialized software environment that provides the essential infrastructure, libraries, and services required to execute a program.

Also called execution environment, software platform, runtime environment, operating system. Examples: Java Virtual Machine (JVM), Node.js runtime, .NET Common Language Runtime (CLR), Python interpreter.
embedding_text: RuntimePlatform (Thing > CreativeWork > SoftwareApplication): A specialized software environment providing the necessary infrastructure, libraries, and services for executing a program. Also called execution environment, software platform, runtime environment, operating system.

label: SaleEvent
comment: Event type: Sales event.
enriched_comment: An event where goods or services are offered for sale, often at reduced prices. Also called sales promotion, discount event, clearance sale, special offer. Examples: a Black Friday sale, an annual warehouse clearance, a seasonal clothing sale, a car dealership's sales event.
embedding_text: SaleEvent (Thing > Event): An event where goods or services are offered for sale, often at reduced prices. Also called sales promotion, discount event, clearance sale, special offer.

label: SatiricalArticle
comment: An [[Article]] whose content is primarily [[satirical]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satire) in nature, i.e. unlikely to be literally true. A satirical article is sometimes but not necessarily also a [[NewsArticle]]. [[ScholarlyArticle]]s are also sometimes satirized.
enriched_comment: An article whose content is primarily satirical, meaning it uses humor, irony, exaggeration, or ridicule to expose and criticize people's stupidity or vices, and is not intended to be literally true. Also called parody article, spoof news, humorous critique, ironic commentary. Examples: an article from The Onion, a piece from a satirical magazine, a political cartoon with extensive text. Distinct from NewsArticle, which aims to report factual information.
embedding_text: SatiricalArticle (Thing > CreativeWork > Article): An article whose content is primarily satirical, meaning it uses humor, irony, exaggeration, or ridicule to expose and criticize people's stupidity or vices, and is not intended to be literally true. Also called parody article, spoof news, humorous critique, ironic commentary.

label: Schedule
comment: A schedule defines a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring [[Event]]. At a minimum a schedule will specify [[repeatFrequency]] which describes the interval between occurrences of the event. Additional information can be provided to specify the schedule more precisely. This includes identifying the day(s) of the week or month when the recurring event will take place, in addition to its start and end time. Schedules may also have start and end dates to indicate when they are active, e.g. to define a limited calendar of events.
enriched_comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.
embedding_text: Schedule (Thing > Intangible): A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine.

label: ScheduleAction
comment:
Scheduling future actions, events, or tasks.

Related actions:

* [[ReserveAction]]: Unlike ReserveAction, ScheduleAction allocates future actions (e.g. an event, a task, etc) towards a time slot / spatial allocation.
enriched_comment: The act of planning and allocating future actions, events, or tasks to specific time slots or spatial allocations. Also called planning, arranging, organizing, booking. Examples: scheduling a doctor's appointment, booking a meeting room, planning a project timeline, arranging a delivery. Distinct from ReserveAction, which implies making a reservation for a specific resource or service.
embedding_text: ScheduleAction (Thing > Action > OrganizeAction > PlanAction): The act of planning and allocating future actions, events, or tasks to specific time slots or spatial allocations. Also called planning, arranging, organizing, booking.

embedding_text: ScholarlyArticle (Thing > CreativeWork > Article): A formal article presenting original research or analysis, typically peer-reviewed and published in an academic journal. Also called academic paper, research article, journal publication, scientific paper.

label: Sculpture

label: SeaBodyOfWater

label: SearchAction

label: SearchRescueOrganization

label: SpecialAnnouncement
comment: A SpecialAnnouncement combines a simple date-stamped textual information update with contextualized Web links and other structured data. It represents an information update made by a locally-oriented organization, for example schools, pharmacies, healthcare providers, community groups, police, local government. For work in progress guidelines on Coronavirus-related markup see [this doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14ikaGCKxo50rRM7nvKSlbUpjyIk2WMQd3IkB1lItlrM/edit#). The motivating scenario for SpecialAnnouncement is the [Coronavirus pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_coronavirus_pandemic), and the initial vocabulary is oriented to this urgent situation. Schema.org expect to improve the markup iteratively as it is deployed and as feedback emerges from use. In addition to our usual [Github entry](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/2490), feedback comments can also be provided in [this document](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fpdFFxk8s87CWwACs53SGkYv3aafSxz_DTtOQxMrBJQ/edit#). While this schema is designed to communicate urgent crisis-related information, it is not the same as an emergency warning technology like [CAP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_Alerting_Protocol), although there may be overlaps. The intent is to cover the kinds of everyday practical information being posted to existing websites during an emergency situation. Several kinds of information can be provided: We encourage the provision of "name", "text", "datePosted", "expires" (if appropriate), "category" and "url" as a simple baseline. It is important to provide a value for "category" where possible, most ideally as a well known URL from Wikipedia or Wikidata. In the case of the 2019-2020 Coronavirus pandemic, this should be "https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2019-20\_coronavirus\_pandemic" or "https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q81068910". For many of the possible properties, values can either be simple links or an inline description, depending on whether a summary is available. For a link, provide just the URL of the appropriate page as the property's value. For an inline description, use a [[WebContent]] type, and provide the url as a property of that, alongside at least a simple "[[text]]" summary of the page. It is unlikely that a single SpecialAnnouncement will need all of the possible properties simultaneously. We expect that in many cases the page referenced might contain more specialized structured data, e.g. contact info, [[openingHours]], [[Event]], [[FAQPage]] etc. By linking to those pages from a [[SpecialAnnouncement]] you can help make it clearer that the events are related to the situation (e.g. Coronavirus) indicated by the [[category]] property of the [[SpecialAnnouncement]]. Many [[SpecialAnnouncement]]s will relate to particular regions and to identifiable local organizations. Use [[spatialCoverage]] for the region, and [[announcementLocation]] to indicate specific [[LocalBusiness]]es and [[CivicStructure]]s. If the announcement affects both a particular region and a specific location (for example, a library closure that serves an entire region), use both [[spatialCoverage]] and [[announcementLocation]]. The [[about]] property can be used to indicate entities that are the focus of the announcement. We now recommend using [[about]] only for representing non-location entities (e.g. a [[Course]] or a [[RadioStation]]). For places, use [[announcementLocation]] and [[spatialCoverage]]. Consumers of this markup should be aware that the initial design encouraged the use of [[about]] for locations too. The basic content of [[SpecialAnnouncement]] is similar to that of an [RSS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RSS) or [Atom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atom_(Web_standard)) feed. For publishers without such feeds, basic feed-like information can be shared by posting [[SpecialAnnouncement]] updates in a page, e.g. using JSON-LD. For sites with Atom/RSS functionality, you can point to a feed with the [[webFeed]] property. This can be a simple URL, or an inline [[DataFeed]] object, with [[encodingFormat]] providing media type information, e.g. "application/rss+xml" or "application/atom+xml".

label: StatisticalPopulation
comment: A StatisticalPopulation is a set of instances of a certain given type that satisfy some set of constraints. The property [[populationType]] is used to specify the type. Any property that can be used on instances of that type can appear on the statistical population. For example, a [[StatisticalPopulation]] representing all [[Person]]s with a [[homeLocation]] of East Podunk California would be described by applying the appropriate [[homeLocation]] and [[populationType]] properties to a [[StatisticalPopulation]] item that stands for that set of people. The properties [[numConstraints]] and [[constraintProperty]] are used to specify which of the populations properties are used to specify the population. Note that the sense of "population" used here is the general sense of a statistical population, and does not imply that the population consists of people. For example, a [[populationType]] of [[Event]] or [[NewsArticle]] could be used. See also [[Observation]], where a [[populationType]] such as [[Person]] or [[Event]] can be indicated directly. In most cases it may be better to use [[StatisticalVariable]] instead of [[StatisticalPopulation]].
enriched_comment: A set of instances of a given type that satisfy specific constraints, used for statistical analysis. Also called statistical group, data population, sample group, target demographic. Examples: all persons with a home location in a specific city, all events occurring in a particular year, all news articles mentioning a certain keyword. Distinct from StatisticalVariable, which represents a measurable metric within a population.
embedding_text: StatisticalPopulation (Thing > Intangible): A set of instances of a given type that satisfy specific constraints, used for statistical analysis. Also called statistical group, data population, sample group, target demographic.

label: StatisticalVariable
comment: [[StatisticalVariable]] represents any type of statistical metric that can be measured at a place and time. The usage pattern for [[StatisticalVariable]] is typically expressed using [[Observation]] with an explicit [[populationType]], which is a type, typically drawn from Schema.org. Each [[StatisticalVariable]] is marked as a [[ConstraintNode]], meaning that some properties (those listed using [[constraintProperty]]) serve in this setting solely to define the statistical variable rather than literally describe a specific person, place or thing. For example, a [[StatisticalVariable]] Median_Height_Person_Female representing the median height of women, could be written as follows: the population type is [[Person]]; the measuredProperty [[height]]; the [[statType]] [[median]]; the [[gender]] [[Female]]. It is important to note that there are many kinds of scientific quantitative observation which are not fully, perfectly or unambiguously described following this pattern, or with solely Schema.org terminology. The approach taken here is designed to allow partial, incremental or minimal description of [[StatisticalVariable]]s, and the use of detailed sets of entity and property IDs from external repositories. The [[measurementMethod]], [[unitCode]] and [[unitText]] properties can also be used to clarify the specific nature and notation of an observed measurement.
enriched_comment: A measurable statistical metric that can be observed at a place and time, defined by a population type and specific constraints. Also called statistical metric, data point, observable quantity, measurement variable. Examples: median height of female persons, average temperature in a city, count of news articles published daily. Distinct from StatisticalPopulation, which is the group being measured, not the measurement itself.
embedding_text: StatisticalVariable (Thing > Intangible > ConstraintNode): A measurable statistical metric that can be observed at a place and time, defined by a population type and specific constraints. Also called statistical metric, data point, observable quantity, measurement variable.

label: SuperficialAnatomy
comment: Anatomical features that can be observed by sight (without dissection), including the form and proportions of the human body as well as surface landmarks that correspond to deeper subcutaneous structures. Superficial anatomy plays an important role in sports medicine, phlebotomy, and other medical specialties as underlying anatomical structures can be identified through surface palpation. For example, during back surgery, superficial anatomy can be used to palpate and count vertebrae to find the site of incision. Or in phlebotomy, superficial anatomy can be used to locate an underlying vein; for example, the median cubital vein can be located by palpating the borders of the cubital fossa (such as the epicondyles of the humerus) and then looking for the superficial signs of the vein, such as size, prominence, ability to refill after depression, and feel of surrounding tissue support. As another example, in a subluxation (dislocation) of the glenohumeral joint, the bony structure becomes pronounced with the deltoid muscle failing to cover the glenohumeral joint allowing the edges of the scapula to be superficially visible. Here, the superficial anatomy is the visible edges of the scapula, implying the underlying dislocation of the joint (the related anatomical structure).
enriched_comment: Anatomical features observable by sight without dissection, including body form, proportions, and surface landmarks corresponding to deeper structures. Also called surface anatomy, external anatomy, visible body structures. Examples: the visible edges of the scapula, the cubital fossa for vein location, the contours of muscles under the skin.

enriched_comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.
embedding_text: Thing: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object.

label: Ticket
comment: Used to describe a ticket to an event, a flight, a bus ride, etc.
enriched_comment: An intangible item used to grant access or confirm a reservation for an event, travel, or service. Also called pass, voucher, entry permit. Examples: a concert ticket, an airline boarding pass, a bus ticket, a movie ticket.
embedding_text: Ticket (Thing > Intangible): An intangible item used to grant access or confirm a reservation for an event, travel, or service. Also called pass, voucher, entry permit.

label: TieAction
comment: The act of reaching a draw in a competitive activity.
enriched_comment: The act of achieving a draw or stalemate in a competitive activity. Also called draw, stalemate, tie game. Examples: two chess players agreeing to a draw, a soccer match ending in a tie, a race where two competitors finish simultaneously.
embedding_text: TieAction (Thing > Action > AchieveAction): The act of achieving a draw or stalemate in a competitive activity. Also called draw, stalemate, tie game.

label: TierBenefitEnumeration
comment: An enumeration of possible benefits as part of a loyalty (members) program.
enriched_comment: An enumeration of specific benefits offered as part of a loyalty or membership program. Also called loyalty program benefit, membership perk, reward tier. Examples: free shipping, early access to sales, exclusive content, dedicated customer support.
embedding_text: TierBenefitEnumeration (Thing > Intangible > Enumeration): An enumeration of specific benefits offered as part of a loyalty or membership program. Also called loyalty program benefit, membership perk, reward tier.

label: Time
comment: A point in time recurring on multiple days in the form hh:mm:ss[Z|(+|-)hh:mm] (see [XML schema for details](http://www.w3.org/TR/xmlschema-2/#time)).
enriched_comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".
embedding_text: Time: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day.

label: TipAction
comment: The act of giving money voluntarily to a beneficiary in recognition of services rendered.
enriched_comment: The act of voluntarily giving money to a beneficiary in appreciation for services rendered. Also called gratuity, tipping, giving a tip. Examples: leaving a tip for a waiter, tipping a taxi driver, giving a barber a gratuity.
embedding_text: TipAction (Thing > Action > TradeAction): The act of voluntarily giving money to a beneficiary in appreciation for services rendered. Also called gratuity, tipping, giving a tip.

label: TireShop
comment: A tire shop.
enriched_comment: A local business specializing in the sale, repair, and installation of vehicle tires. Also called tire store, auto tire center, wheel shop. Examples: Discount Tire, a local independent tire dealer, a car service center with a tire department.
embedding_text: TireShop (Thing > Organization > LocalBusiness > Store): A local business specializing in the sale, repair, and installation of vehicle tires. Also called tire store, auto tire center, wheel shop.

label: TouristAttraction
comment: A tourist attraction. In principle any Thing can be a [[TouristAttraction]], from a [[Mountain]] and [[LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings]] to a [[LocalBusiness]]. This Type can be used on its own to describe a general [[TouristAttraction]], or be used as an [[additionalType]] to add tourist attraction properties to any other type. (See examples below)
enriched_comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.
embedding_text: TouristAttraction (Thing > Place): A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark.

label: TouristDestination
comment: A tourist destination. In principle any [[Place]] can be a [[TouristDestination]] from a [[City]], Region or [[Country]] to an [[AmusementPark]] or [[Hotel]]. This Type can be used on its own to describe a general [[TouristDestination]], or be used as an [[additionalType]] to add tourist relevant properties to any other [[Place]]. A [[TouristDestination]] is defined as a [[Place]] that contains, or is colocated with, one or more [[TouristAttraction]]s, often linked by a similar theme or interest to a particular [[touristType]]. The [UNWTO](http://www2.unwto.org/) defines Destination (main destination of a tourism trip) as the place visited that is central to the decision to take the trip. (See examples below.)
enriched_comment: A place, region, or area that is a primary focus for tourism, often containing multiple tourist attractions. Also called travel destination, vacation spot, tourist region. Examples: Paris, the Grand Canyon, the Caribbean islands, a specific resort town. Distinct from TouristAttraction, which is a specific point of interest within a destination.
embedding_text: TouristDestination (Thing > Place): A place, region, or area that is a primary focus for tourism, often containing multiple tourist attractions. Also called travel destination, vacation spot, tourist region.

label: TouristInformationCenter
comment: A tourist information center.
enriched_comment: A local business providing information and services to tourists. Also called visitor center, tourist office, travel information point. Examples: a city visitor center, a national park information booth, a regional tourism office.
embedding_text: TouristInformationCenter (Thing > Organization > LocalBusiness): A local business providing information and services to tourists. Also called visitor center, tourist office, travel information point.

label: TouristTrip
comment: A tourist trip. A created itinerary of visits to one or more places of interest ([[TouristAttraction]]/[[TouristDestination]]) often linked by a similar theme, geographic area, or interest to a particular [[touristType]]. The [UNWTO](http://www2.unwto.org/) defines tourism trip as the Trip taken by visitors. (See examples below.)
enriched_comment: An itinerary or journey undertaken by visitors for tourism purposes, often involving visits to multiple places of interest. Also called vacation itinerary, travel plan, sightseeing tour. Examples: a two-week European tour, a weekend getaway to a national park, a cruise itinerary.
embedding_text: TouristTrip (Thing > Intangible > Trip): An itinerary or journey undertaken by visitors for tourism purposes, often involving visits to multiple places of interest. Also called vacation itinerary, travel plan, sightseeing tour.

label: ToyStore
comment: A toy store.
enriched_comment: A local business specializing in the sale of toys and games. Also called toy shop, game store, children's store. Examples: Toys 'R' Us, a local independent toy boutique, a department store's toy section.
embedding_text: ToyStore (Thing > Organization > LocalBusiness > Store): A local business specializing in the sale of toys and games. Also called toy shop, game store, children's store.

label: TrackAction
comment:
An agent tracks an object for updates.

Related actions:

* [[FollowAction]]: Unlike FollowAction, TrackAction refers to the interest on the location of innanimates objects.
* [[SubscribeAction]]: Unlike SubscribeAction, TrackAction refers to the interest on the location of innanimate objects.
enriched_comment: The act of monitoring an inanimate object for updates or changes in its location or status. Also called monitoring, tracking, observing. Examples: tracking a package delivery, monitoring a flight's progress, tracking a lost phone.
embedding_text: TrackAction (Thing > Action > FindAction): The act of monitoring an inanimate object for updates or changes in its location or status. Also called monitoring, tracking, observing.

label: TradeAction
comment: The act of participating in an exchange of goods and services for monetary compensation. An agent trades an object, product or service with a participant in exchange for a one time or periodic payment.
enriched_comment: The act of exchanging goods or services for monetary compensation. Also called commerce, transaction, selling. Examples: a business selling products to customers, a consultant providing services for a fee, an artist selling their artwork.
embedding_text: TradeAction (Thing > Action): The act of exchanging goods or services for monetary compensation. Also called commerce, transaction, selling.

label: TrainReservation
comment: A reservation for train travel.\n\nNote: This type is for information about actual reservations, e.g. in confirmation emails or HTML pages with individual confirmations of reservations. For offers of tickets, use [[Offer]].
enriched_comment: A reservation specifically for travel on a commercial train line. Also called train booking, rail reservation, seat booking. Examples: a reservation for a high-speed train, a sleeper car booking, a ticket for a scenic rail journey.
embedding_text: TrainReservation (Thing > Intangible > Reservation): A reservation specifically for travel on a commercial train line. Also called train booking, rail reservation, seat booking.

label: TrainStation
comment: A train station.
enriched_comment: A civic structure serving as a designated stop for trains, where passengers can board or alight. Also called railway station, rail depot, terminal station. Examples: Grand Central Terminal, London King's Cross, a local commuter rail station.
embedding_text: TrainStation (Thing > Place > CivicStructure): A civic structure serving as a designated stop for trains, where passengers can board or alight. Also called railway station, rail depot, terminal station.

label: TrainTrip
comment: A trip on a commercial train line.
enriched_comment: A journey or itinerary undertaken using a commercial train line. Also called rail journey, train travel, railway trip. Examples: a cross-country train journey, a daily commute by train, a scenic train ride through the mountains.
embedding_text: TrainTrip (Thing > Intangible > Trip): A journey or itinerary undertaken using a commercial train line. Also called rail journey, train travel, railway trip.

label: TransferAction
comment: The act of transferring/moving (abstract or concrete) animate or inanimate objects from one place to another.
enriched_comment: The act of moving an object, whether animate or inanimate, from one location to another. Also called move, transport, relocate. Examples: transferring funds between bank accounts, moving furniture to a new house, transferring a patient to another hospital.
embedding_text: TransferAction (Thing > Action): The act of moving an object, whether animate or inanimate, from one location to another. Also called move, transport, relocate.

label: TravelAction
comment: The act of traveling from a fromLocation to a destination by a specified mode of transport, optionally with participants.
enriched_comment: The act of moving from a starting location to a destination using a specified mode of transport. Also called journey, commute, voyage. Examples: traveling by car from home to work, flying from New York to London, taking a bus to another city.
embedding_text: TravelAction (Thing > Action > MoveAction): The act of moving from a starting location to a destination using a specified mode of transport. Also called journey, commute, voyage.

label: TravelAgency
comment: A travel agency.
enriched_comment: A local business that assists individuals and groups in planning and booking travel arrangements. Also called travel agent, tour operator, booking agency. Examples: Expedia, a local independent travel agency, a corporate travel management company.
embedding_text: TravelAgency (Thing > Organization > LocalBusiness): A local business that assists individuals and groups in planning and booking travel arrangements. Also called travel agent, tour operator, booking agency.

label: TreatmentIndication
comment: An indication for treating an underlying condition, symptom, etc.
enriched_comment: A medical indication specifying the appropriate use of a treatment for an underlying health condition or symptom. Also called therapeutic indication, medical use, treatment rationale. Examples: an antibiotic indicated for bacterial infections, a pain reliever indicated for headaches, a specific therapy for cancer.
embedding_text: TreatmentIndication (Thing > MedicalEntity > MedicalIndication): A medical indication specifying the appropriate use of a treatment for an underlying health condition or symptom. Also called therapeutic indication, medical use, treatment rationale.

label: Trip
comment: A trip or journey. An itinerary of visits to one or more places.
enriched_comment: A general term for a journey or itinerary involving visits to one or more places. Also called journey, travel, excursion. Examples: a business trip, a family vacation, a day trip to the beach.
embedding_text: Trip (Thing > Intangible): A general term for a journey or itinerary involving visits to one or more places. Also called journey, travel, excursion.

label: TypeAndQuantityNode
comment: A structured value indicating the quantity, unit of measurement, and business function of goods included in a bundle offer.
enriched_comment: A structured value indicating the quantity, unit of measurement, and business function of goods within a bundle offer. Also called quantity specification, offer item details, bundle component. Examples: "3 kg of apples for sale", "2 units of product X as a bonus", "1 liter of milk in a grocery bundle".
embedding_text: TypeAndQuantityNode (Thing > Intangible > StructuredValue): A structured value indicating the quantity, unit of measurement, and business function of goods within a bundle offer. Also called quantity specification, offer item details, bundle component.

label: UKNonprofitType
comment: UKNonprofitType: Non-profit organization type originating from the United Kingdom.
enriched_comment: An enumeration of specific non-profit organization types recognized within the United Kingdom. Also called UK charity type, British non-profit category, UK voluntary sector classification. Examples: a registered charity, a community interest company (CIC), a benevolent society.
embedding_text: UKNonprofitType (Thing > Intangible > Enumeration > NonprofitType): An enumeration of specific non-profit organization types recognized within the United Kingdom. Also called UK charity type, British non-profit category, UK voluntary sector classification.

label: URL
comment: Data type: URL.
enriched_comment: A data type representing a Uniform Resource Locator, which specifies the address of a resource on the internet. Also called web address, link, internet address. Examples: "https://schema.org", "ftp://example.com/file.zip", "mailto:info@example.com".
embedding_text: URL (Text): A data type representing a Uniform Resource Locator, which specifies the address of a resource on the internet. Also called web address, link, internet address.

label: USNonprofitType
comment: USNonprofitType: Non-profit organization type originating from the United States.
enriched_comment: An enumeration of specific non-profit organization types recognized within the United States. Also called US charity type, American non-profit category, US voluntary sector classification. Examples: a 501(c)(3) organization, a public charity, a private foundation.
embedding_text: USNonprofitType (Thing > Intangible > Enumeration > NonprofitType): An enumeration of specific non-profit organization types recognized within the United States. Also called US charity type, American non-profit category, US voluntary sector classification.

label: UnRegisterAction
comment:
The act of un-registering from a service.

Related actions:

* [[RegisterAction]]: antonym of UnRegisterAction.
* [[LeaveAction]]: Unlike LeaveAction, UnRegisterAction implies that you are unregistering from a service you were previously registered, rather than leaving a team/group of people.
enriched_comment: The act of formally removing oneself from a service, membership, or registration. Also called unsubscribe, deregister, cancel registration. Examples: unregistering from a website, unsubscribing from a newsletter, canceling a gym membership. Distinct from LeaveAction, which implies departing a group or team rather than a service.
embedding_text: UnRegisterAction (Thing > Action > InteractAction): The act of formally removing oneself from a service, membership, or registration. Also called unsubscribe, deregister, cancel registration.

label: UnitPriceSpecification
comment: The price asked for a given offer by the respective organization or person.
enriched_comment: A structured value detailing the price asked for a specific offer by an organization or person. Also called price details, cost specification, offer price. Examples: "$10.99 per item", "€50 per hour", "£2.50 per unit".
embedding_text: UnitPriceSpecification (Thing > Intangible > StructuredValue > PriceSpecification): A structured value detailing the price asked for a specific offer by an organization or person. Also called price details, cost specification, offer price.

label: UpdateAction
comment: The act of managing by changing/editing the state of the object.
enriched_comment: The act of managing or changing the state or content of an object. Also called modify, edit, revise. Examples: updating a software application, editing a document, changing a profile picture.
embedding_text: UpdateAction (Thing > Action): The act of managing or changing the state or content of an object. Also called modify, edit, revise.

label: UseAction
comment: The act of applying an object to its intended purpose.
enriched_comment: The act of applying an object to its intended purpose or function. Also called utilize, employ, operate. Examples: using a tool to fix something, consuming food, wearing clothes.
embedding_text: UseAction (Thing > Action > ConsumeAction): The act of applying an object to its intended purpose or function. Also called utilize, employ, operate.

label: UserBlocks
comment: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use [[Action]]-based vocabulary, alongside types such as [[Comment]].
enriched_comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of blocking another user or content. Also called user block, content block, account block. Examples: a user blocking another user on a social media platform, blocking a specific website, blocking notifications from an app.
embedding_text: UserBlocks (Thing > Event > UserInteraction): An outdated type representing a user's interaction of blocking another user or content. Also called user block, content block, account block.

comment: UserInteraction and its subtypes is an old way of talking about users interacting with pages. It is generally better to use [[Action]]-based vocabulary, alongside types such as [[Comment]].

embedding_text: UserCheckins (Thing > Event > UserInteraction): An outdated type representing a user's interaction of checking into a location or event. Also called user check-in, location check-in, event attendance.

label: UserComments
